front_en/abstract.tex:2:This dissertation presents \textbf{MutBench}, a hotspot-detection benchmark that systematically compares 10 biological information types (20 scoring formulas) $\times$ 14 detection families (39 variants) $\times$ 11 RNA viruses = 8{,}580 evaluations. The headline result: the optimal information source is pathogen-dependent, with the scoring~$\times$~pathogen interaction ($\omega^2 = 0.296$, 95\% CI [0.195, 0.333]) as the largest modeled variance component, and HIV-1 vaccine-escape enrichment of $7.19\times$ (Bonferroni $p = 2.5 \times 10^{-16}$) as the primary external anchor.
front_en/abstract.tex:4:Detecting mutation hotspots in viral genomes is essential for variant surveillance and vaccine design, yet existing approaches have relied almost exclusively on mutation frequency and Shannon entropy, leaving comparatively unexplored a rich landscape of complementary information sources (phylogenetic selection signals, protein language models, structural features). Concurrent fitness-regression benchmarks (ViroGym, EVEREST~v3, ProteinGym~v1.3) target per-variant prediction; MutBench is the broadest \emph{region-level hotspot-detection} benchmark to date.
front_en/abstract.tex:8:(3) a two-stage experimental design in which Stage~1 conducts in-depth analysis on SARS-CoV-2 and Stage~2 performs the large-scale cross-pathogen comparison.
front_en/abstract.tex:10:Stage~1 validates the framework on SARS-CoV-2 (MutClust-Hybrid hotspot-score 0.778). Stage~2 establishes that the optimal information source varies systematically across pathogens: $\omega^2_{\text{scoring}\times\text{pathogen}} = 0.296$ (CI [0.195, 0.333]; 6-category aggregation gives $\omega^2 = 0.103$ as a collinearity-robust lower bound; within-cell residual $\omega^2 \approx 0.39$). Friedman test shows no universally best combination ($\chi^2 = 7.69$, $p = 0.990$), and LOPO yields 0/11 exact matches with a 0.265 oracle-vs-generalized MCC gap (LOPO 0/11 alone is null-consistent under permutation; the conclusion rests on the interaction effect plus the vaccine-escape audit, not on LOPO in isolation).
front_en/abstract.tex:11:Contribution 3 is two-part: \textit{(3a) Multi-source integration infrastructure} ---a 4-feature core captures $\approx$98\% (97.6\%) of the 10-feature ensemble; EqualWeight integration achieves H3N2 enrichment 4.012$\times$ ($p = 0.0023$). \textit{(3b) External validation, anchored on HIV-1} ---under a three-tier evidence rule (Bonferroni survival~$\times$~Layer~A overlap < 33\%), HIV-1 is the primary anchor with direct novel-only Fisher enrichment $7.16\text{--}8.24\times$ on the 37 Layer-A-disjoint positions (worst-case $p = 5 \times 10^{-12}$); H3N2 ($9.36\times$, 69\% overlap) is a self-consistency check; SARS-CoV-2 ($7.63\times$) is exploratory after Bonferroni. Validation is restricted to 3/11 pathogens (2{,}340 evaluations) by availability of curated antibody-escape annotations.
front_en/abstract.tex:13:A systematic analysis of the 20 scoring types spanning six information categories (frequency, MSA-derived, phylogenetic, structural, AI-based, and composite) reveals 9 distinct optimal information types across 11 pathogens: FUBAR phylogenetic selection scores achieve the highest MCC for H3N2 (0.534), protein language model scores dominate for SARS-CoV-2 and RSV, and homoplasy scores excel for Norovirus.
front_en/abstract.tex:14:Multi-source integration further reduces the experimental search space for hotspot validation, achieving 4.012$\times$ vaccine escape enrichment for H3N2 ($p = 0.0023$), while a compact 4-feature core captures $\approx$98\% (97.6\%) of full-ensemble performance.
front_en/abstract.tex:17:\noindent\textbf{Keywords}: mutation hotspot detection, MutBench, biological information types, viral genomics, multi-source information analysis, pathogen-dependent optimality, SARS-CoV-2, Deep Mutational Scanning

chapters_en/ch1_introduction.tex:9:SARS-CoV-2, which emerged in late 2019, caused more than 700 million confirmed cases worldwide, reaffirming the critical importance of viral genome analysis~\cite{harvey2021tracking}.
chapters_en/ch1_introduction.tex:33:Existing computational approaches for hotspot detection have relied predominantly on two types of information: mutation frequency and Shannon entropy. While these capture the most direct signals of mutational enrichment, they fail to distinguish biologically meaningful hotspots from founder-effect artifacts and cannot leverage the growing wealth of complementary information sources---including phylogenetic selection signals, protein language model predictions, structural features, and deep mutational scanning data. Concurrent benchmarks evaluate per-variant fitness regression on overlapping virus panels (notably ViroGym~\cite{virogym2026}, 13 viruses / 79 DMS / 7 phenotypes; EVEREST~v3~\cite{gurev2026everest_v3}, 45 DMS / 31 forecasting clades / 40 WHO priority viruses; ProteinGym~\cite{notin2023proteingym,notin2025proteingym_v13}, 217 DMS / 90+ baselines), but none has performed a region-level hotspot-detection comparison that systematically decomposes which biological information types are most effective for which pathogens, leaving researchers to default to frequency-based approaches regardless of the virus under study.
chapters_en/ch1_introduction.tex:42:In the first stage (\textit{sequence collection}), viral genomes from infected individuals are sequenced over weeks to months at research institutions worldwide and deposited in public databases such as GISAID and NCBI GenBank; for SARS-CoV-2, millions of sequences have been accumulated since 2020, while for influenza, tens of thousands of sequences span several decades.
chapters_en/ch1_introduction.tex:59:The bootstrap test, MutClust's sole validation method, is a self-referential approach that can only confirm the statistical significance of detected clusters; it cannot verify whether those clusters correspond to biologically meaningful functional regions.
chapters_en/ch1_introduction.tex:64:Convergent evolution sites are mutations that independently arise at the same genomic position in multiple lineages within the same viral species; for example, mutations at Spike position 484 emerged independently across multiple SARS-CoV-2 lineages: E484K (glutamic acid to lysine) in Beta, Gamma, and Mu, and E484A (glutamic acid to alanine) in Omicron.
chapters_en/ch1_introduction.tex:82:  \item A two-stage experimental design: Stage~1 for in-depth SARS-CoV-2 analysis; Stage~2 for large-scale comparison across 11 RNA viruses (20 scoring formulas $\times$ 39 detection parameter variants from 14 families $\times$ 11 pathogens = 8{,}580 evaluations, with information-type analysis across all 11 pathogens).
chapters_en/ch1_introduction.tex:85:  \item \textbf{Identify the dominant factor in hotspot detection performance}: Through factorial Analysis of Variance (ANOVA), Friedman test, and Leave-One-Pathogen-Out (LOPO) cross-validation, determine whether the optimal scoring method differs across pathogens and quantify the relative importance of scoring type, detection method, and pathogen as sources of performance variance (see Chapter~\ref{ch:results}).
chapters_en/ch1_introduction.tex:90:Figure~\ref{fig:research_overview} summarizes the overall research flow: from identifying the information limitation (reliance on frequency/entropy), through systematic comparison of 10 information types via MutBench, to the key finding that the optimal information source differs by pathogen, culminating in external vaccine-escape validation on a Layer~A-disjoint subset (HIV-1, 7.19$\times$, Bonferroni-significant) as the primary anchor for practical impact.

chapters_en/ch1_introduction.tex:131:\caption{Research overview. The study proceeds from identifying the information limitation (reliance on frequency/entropy) through systematic comparison of 10 information types via MutBench, to the key finding that the optimal information source differs by pathogen, culminating in external vaccine-escape validation on a Layer~A-disjoint subset (HIV-1, Bonferroni-significant) as the primary anchor for practical impact.}
chapters_en/ch1_introduction.tex:142:MutBench is the broadest hotspot-detection benchmark to date, complementing concurrent fitness-regression benchmarks (ViroGym~\cite{virogym2026}, EVEREST~v3~\cite{gurev2026everest_v3}, ProteinGym v1.3~\cite{notin2025proteingym_v13}) by targeting region-level detection rather than per-variant fitness, and is designed to answer the question: \emph{which biological information source is most effective for which pathogen?}
chapters_en/ch1_introduction.tex:143:It organizes 10 information types into 20 scoring formulas across 6 categories (frequency, MSA-derived, phylogenetic, structural, AI-based, and composite), defines a three-layer ground truth framework (convergent evolution positives as Layer~A, purifying selection negatives as Layer~B, DMS experimental fitness as Layer~C), introduces the hotspot-score composite metric, and presents a two-stage experimental design combining in-depth SARS-CoV-2 analysis with a large-scale comparison across eleven pathogens.
chapters_en/ch1_introduction.tex:145:\textbf{Contribution 2. Statistical demonstration that the optimal biological information source differs fundamentally across pathogens ($\omega^2_{\text{scoring} \times \text{pathogen}} = 0.296$), with 9 distinct optimal information types across 11 pathogens and no cross-pathogen generalization (LOPO 0/11).}
chapters_en/ch1_introduction.tex:146:All eleven pathogens exhibited different best-performing combinations (LOPO cross-validation: 0/11 matches), with 9 distinct best-performing scoring types observed---including FUBAR phylogenetic selection scores for H3N2, protein language model scores for SARS-CoV-2 and RSV, and homoplasy for Norovirus.
chapters_en/ch1_introduction.tex:147:The Friedman test ($p = 0.990$) showed no reliably superior combination across all pathogens, consistent with pathogen-dependent optimality.
chapters_en/ch1_introduction.tex:148:The scoring~$\times$~pathogen interaction is the largest modeled variance component ($\omega^2 = 0.296$, 95\% cluster-bootstrap CI [0.195, 0.333]; 6-category aggregation gives $\omega^2 = 0.103$ as a collinearity-robust lower bound). The conclusion rests on the interaction effect plus the vaccine-escape audit; LOPO 0/11 alone is null-consistent under permutation (Chapter~\ref{ch:results} Table~\ref{tab:9pathogen_anova}).
chapters_en/ch1_introduction.tex:150:\textbf{Contribution 3 (two-part).} \textit{(3a) Multi-source integration infrastructure}: a compact 4-feature core (homoplasy, pLDDT, entropy, frequency) captures $\approx$98\% (97.6\%, 0.081/0.083) of the full 10-feature ensemble performance, and the EqualWeight integration achieves a statistically significant 4.012-fold H3N2 enrichment ($p = 0.0023$) where single-feature approaches fail. \textit{(3b) Externally-valid vaccine-escape enrichment, anchored on HIV-1}: the Layer-A-disjoint subset of HIV-1 escape positions (37 of 45) yields a direct novel-only enrichment of $7.16\text{--}8.24\times$ (worst-case Bonferroni-adjusted Fisher $p = 5.0 \times 10^{-12}$); H3N2's 9.36$\times$ is a self-consistency check (69\% Layer~A overlap); SARS-CoV-2 is exploratory after multiple-comparison correction.
chapters_en/ch1_introduction.tex:151:A systematic analysis of 10 biological information types---spanning sequence statistics, phylogenetic signals, protein language models, structural properties, and chemical characteristics---reveals that the most discriminative single feature (per-feature AUC) differs across pathogens (e.g., homoplasy for Norovirus, pLDDT for H3N2, ESM-2 for SARS-CoV-2), complementing the Stage~2 MCC-optimal scoring results in Contribution~2.
chapters_en/ch1_introduction.tex:152:Feature ablation identifies a 4-feature core (homoplasy, pLDDT, entropy, frequency) that captures $\approx$98\% (97.6\%) of integrated performance.
chapters_en/ch1_introduction.tex:153:Multi-source integration reduces the experimental search space for hotspot validation, achieving H3N2 vaccine escape enrichment of 4.012$\times$ ($p = 0.0023$), while pathogen-optimized scoring achieves up to 7.19$\times$ enrichment for HIV-1 on the Layer~A-disjoint (novel) portion of the escape set (Bonferroni-corrected $p = 2.5 \times 10^{-16}$); the headline H3N2 9.36$\times$ is dominated by Layer~A-overlap positions and, restricted to the 9 novel positions, drops to 7.19$\times$ with Fisher $p = 0.132$ (not significant). The benchmark's external validation is therefore primarily carried by HIV-1, with H3N2/SARS-CoV-2 providing self-consistency and exploratory evidence respectively (see Chapter~\ref{ch:results} Table~\ref{tab:vaccine_escape_stage3} for the full circularity audit).
chapters_en/ch1_introduction.tex:165:Section~3.1 describes the materials (target pathogens and sequence data). Section~3.2 presents the methods: the framework overview and three-layer ground truth (Sections~3.2.1--3.2.2), the Stage~1 SARS-CoV-2 analysis design including MutClust variants and the hotspot-score metric (Section~3.2.3), the Stage~2 cross-pathogen benchmark design with 20 scoring types and 14 detection families (Section~3.2.4), and the evaluation metrics and statistical analysis design (Section~3.2.5).
chapters_en/ch1_introduction.tex:167:\textbf{Chapter~\ref{ch:results}, Experimental Results} reports the experimental results organized into five sections: Single-Pathogen Benchmark (synthetic data comparison, multi-ground truth evaluation, real GISAID validation, and external methods comparison on SARS-CoV-2), Robustness Validation (statistical validation, sensitivity analysis, temporal generalization, and indel exclusion), Cross-Pathogen Validation (H3N2 validation, 3D structural analysis, phylogenetic simulation, and ESM-2 cross-paradigm validation), the Cross-Pathogen Large-Scale Benchmark (ANOVA, Friedman test, LOPO cross-validation), and Information-Type Analysis (feature ablation, ground truth heterogeneity, search space reduction, and multi-source integration across 11 pathogens).
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:6:The overall pipeline processes multiple sequence alignment (MSA) data from 11 RNA viruses through 20 scoring types and 14 detection method families spanning 5 categories (threshold-based, signal processing, density/clustering, statistical, and adaptive window), with 39 parameter variants, evaluating results against a 3-layer ground truth system using the hotspot-score composite metric and Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC).
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:7:The evaluation follows a two-stage main design with a Stage~3 information-integration layer: Stage~1 conducts in-depth analysis on SARS-CoV-2 to validate the framework components, Stage~2 extends the evaluation to all 11 pathogens for the large-scale cross-pathogen MCC comparison, and Stage~3 (Section~\ref{subsec:stage3_methods}) decomposes the resulting performance by information type via per-feature AUC, ablation, Random Forest, and vaccine-escape cross-validation.
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:10:The experimental design is then presented in two stages: Stage~1 (Section~\ref{subsec:stage1}) focuses on SARS-CoV-2 in-depth analysis including MutClust variant comparison and the hotspot-score metric, while Stage~2 (Section~\ref{sec:stage2}) extends to the 11-pathogen cross-pathogen benchmark with 20 scoring types and 14 detection families.
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:22:(1)~\textit{Respiratory viruses}: SARS-CoV-2 (Spike, 1,259 AA), MERS-CoV (Spike, 1,330 AA), RSV (F protein, 550 AA), Influenza A H3N2 (HA, 543 AA), and Influenza B (HA, 560 AA);
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:23:(2)~\textit{Blood-borne/sexually transmitted}: HIV-1 (Env gp120, 450 AA) and HCV (E2, 340 AA);
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:27:\textit{Note: all amino acid lengths above refer to post-truncation alignment lengths used in the benchmark; full-length protein sequences may differ (e.g., SARS-CoV-2 Spike full length is 1{,}273 AA, MERS-CoV Spike 1{,}353 AA, Rabies G 524 AA, EV-A71 VP1 297 AA).}
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:28:These 11 pathogens span substitution rates from $\sim$10$^{-3}$ (HIV-1, SARS-CoV-2) to $\sim$10$^{-4}$ (Rabies) substitutions/site/year, alignment lengths from 261 to 1,330 AA, and evolutionary patterns from rapid antigenic drift (H3N2) to epochal evolution (Norovirus).
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:39:\paragraph{SARS-CoV-2 (Spike, 1,259 AA).}
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:40:A betacoronavirus (family \textit{Coronaviridae}) that caused the COVID-19 pandemic (2019--present), SARS-CoV-2 serves as the primary reference pathogen for this benchmark.
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:42:SARS-CoV-2 evolves at ${\sim}1 \times 10^{-3}$ substitutions/site/year for the Spike gene, with its relatively shallow pandemic phylogeny ($\sim$5 years in our dataset, 2019--2024) creating strong founder effects (e.g., D614G) while convergent evolution at immune evasion sites (E484K, N501Y) provides clear Layer~A ground truth.
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:43:The low unique sequence ratio (753/4,982 = 15.1\%) reflects massive sequencing of identical or near-identical lineages during the early pandemic.
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:45:SARS-CoV-2 was selected as the anchor pathogen because it offers the richest ground truth data across all three layers.
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:48:A betacoronavirus (family \textit{Coronaviridae}) first identified in Saudi Arabia in 2012 and causing Middle East Respiratory Syndrome, MERS-CoV has a case fatality rate of $\sim$35\%, far exceeding that of SARS-CoV-2.
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:50:MERS-CoV evolves more slowly than SARS-CoV-2, with a substitution rate of ${\sim}0.9 \times 10^{-3}$ substitutions/site/year, and sporadic zoonotic spillovers from dromedary camels produce limited human-to-human transmission chains.
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:61:\paragraph{Influenza A H3N2 (HA, 543 AA).}
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:62:Influenza A H3N2 (family \textit{Orthomyxoviridae}) has circulated in humans since the 1968 pandemic and remains a major driver of seasonal influenza morbidity and mortality.
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:64:H3N2 exhibits rapid antigenic drift at ${\sim}4 \times 10^{-3}$ substitutions/site/year in HA, one of the highest rates among RNA viruses, driven by strong immune selection on the globular head domain.
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:66:H3N2 was selected as the archetypal rapidly drifting pathogen whose well-characterized antigenic sites provide robust Layer~A ground truth.
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:70:The HA protein serves the same receptor-binding and membrane fusion roles as in influenza A, but Influenza B evolves more slowly (${\sim}2 \times 10^{-3}$ substitutions/site/year) with two co-circulating lineages (Victoria and Yamagata) that diverged in the 1980s.
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:72:Influenza B was selected to contrast with H3N2: both are segmented negative-sense RNA viruses targeting HA, but Influenza B's slower drift rate and dual-lineage structure test whether detection methods generalize across different evolutionary tempos within the same virus family.
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:77:\paragraph{HIV-1 (Env gp120, 450 AA).}
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:80:HIV-1 mutates at ${\sim}2.5 \times 10^{-3}$ substitutions/site/year (one of the highest rates among the benchmark pathogens; EV-A71 is comparable~\cite{sanjuan2010viral}), with extensive within-host and between-host diversity generating up to 35\% amino acid divergence across subtypes.
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:82:HIV-1 was selected as the extreme end of the mutation rate spectrum, testing whether detection methods remain effective under very high sequence diversity where nearly every position is variable.
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:131:FASTA sequences for each pathogen were collected from NCBI GenBank by querying each target protein name (e.g., ``SARS-CoV-2 spike glycoprotein'') with filters for complete coding sequences, excluding partial sequences and laboratory-derived constructs. No date range restriction was applied; all available sequences as of December 2024 were downloaded. Sequences with $>$5\% ambiguous bases (N) were removed, and identical sequences were deduplicated (the ``Unique seq.'' column in Table~\ref{tab:pathogen_data} reflects post-deduplication counts). Multiple sequence alignment (MSA) was performed for each surface protein (SARS-CoV-2: Spike, H3N2: HA, HIV-1: Env gp120, etc.) using MAFFT v7.505~\cite{katoh2013mafft} with the \texttt{--auto} mode, followed by computation of per-position mutation frequency and entropy.

chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:276:\caption{3-Layer Ground Truth Framework. Layer~A (convergent evolution) defines true positives for MCC computation, Layer~B (purifying selection) defines true negatives for constrained FPR, and Layer~C (DMS fitness) provides independent experimental validation. The three layers capture orthogonal dimensions of mutational importance.}
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:287:\subsubsection{Layer A: Adaptive Positive Selection}
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:290:For example, mutations at Spike position 484 in SARS-CoV-2---enabling immune evasion by altering the antibody binding surface---emerged independently across multiple lineages: E484K (glutamic acid to lysine) in Beta, Gamma, and Mu, and E484A (glutamic acid to alanine) in Omicron, each descending from different ancestral branches of the phylogenetic tree. This repeated independent emergence at the same position provides strong evidence of positive selection.
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:296:For each pathogen, Layer~A positions were compiled from published studies (Table~\ref{tab:gt_positions}, rightmost column). The construction is operationally heterogeneous across the 11 pathogens: SARS-CoV-2 and H3N2 use phylogenetically confirmed convergent evolution sites ($\geq$3 independent lineages); Norovirus uses epochal-variant positions; HCV uses the hypervariable regions HVR1/HVR2 (diversifying selection rather than convergence); and the remaining seven pathogens use literature-reported immune-escape position lists. No single computational criterion is applied uniformly---the framework adopts the per-pathogen literature-curated list to maximize biological fidelity, accepting in exchange that ``Layer~A'' denotes a heterogeneous adaptive-selection union (convergent evolution $\cup$ immune escape $\cup$ HVR membership) rather than a single algorithmic construct. This heterogeneity is revisited in Chapter~\ref{ch:discussion} where its quantitative impact on the headline $\omega^2 = 0.296$ is discussed; for the purposes of this chapter the operational definition is: \emph{Layer~A is the union of literature-curated positive/diversifying-selection positions per the references in Table~\ref{tab:gt_positions}}.
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:297:For example, SARS-CoV-2 Layer~A positions (e.g., E484, N501, L452, K417) were identified by Carabelli et al.~\cite{carabelli2023convergent} through phylogenetic analysis showing independent emergence across Alpha, Beta, Gamma, Delta, and Omicron lineages.
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:310:For SARS-CoV-2, the 154 Layer~B positions include the HR1 (AA 912--984) and HR2 (AA 1,163--1,213) heptad repeats and structural cysteine residues, identified from the cryo-EM structure~\cite{wrapp2020cryo} and conservation analysis.
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:315:For six pathogens with available Deep Mutational Scanning (DMS) experimental data---SARS-CoV-2~\cite{dadonaite2023dms}, H3N2, HIV-1, RSV, Rabies, and EV-A71---experimentally measured fitness effects are used as ground truth.
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:316:Unlike Layer~A (which infers importance from evolutionary patterns) and Layer~B (which infers importance from structural conservation), Layer~C provides direct experimental measurements: in DMS experiments, every possible single amino acid substitution at every position is physically constructed in the laboratory, and its effect on a quantifiable phenotype (e.g., cell entry efficiency for SARS-CoV-2, replicative fitness for H3N2) is measured.
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:319:The DMS phenotypes measured differ by pathogen: cell entry fitness for SARS-CoV-2~\cite{dadonaite2024nature} and RSV~\cite{simonich2026rsvdms}, viral replicative fitness for H3N2~\cite{lee2018h3n2dms}, viral growth in cell culture for HIV-1~\cite{haddox2018hiv1dms}, G-protein-mediated cell entry for Rabies~\cite{aditham2025rabies}, and replicative fitness for EV-A71~\cite{bakhache2025eva71}. Table~\ref{tab:dms_preprocessing} summarises the per-pathogen DMS preprocessing conventions adopted in this benchmark; cell-line and replicate-aggregation choices follow the released-source defaults except where noted.

chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:346:\textbf{Layer A/B overlap handling.}
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:347:In RSV (positions 148, 152) and Influenza B (positions 141, 194), overlapping positions exist between Layer A and Layer B.
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:349:In MCC evaluation, these positions are prioritized as Layer A (positive) and excluded from the Layer B (negative) set.
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:352:\textbf{Layer A/C conflict handling.}
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:354:(1)~\textbf{Layer~A $\to$ MCC}: Layer~A positions are treated as positives and all other positions as negatives; Layer~C membership does not affect the MCC calculation.
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:357:Thus a position that is Layer~A-positive but Layer~C-negative counts as a true positive for the MCC metric (it is evolutionarily hot by construction) and a true negative for the DMS F1 metric (it is not among the top 20\% of measured fitness effects) simultaneously, without internal contradiction. This is consistent with the design choice that no single universal ``hotspot'' label is asserted; rather, the benchmark reports performance against each operationalization of hotspot-ness independently.

chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:391:\textbf{HIV-1 Layer~A count reconciliation}: this table reports the literature-curated Layer~A count of \textbf{23} positions (Moore \& Williamson 2015 baseline) which is the canonical narrative reference. The downstream operational alignment-QC count of \textbf{26} positions (used by AUC computation in Table~\ref{tab:gt_heterogeneity} and the positive-rate footnote in Table~\ref{tab:design_characteristics}) adds three positions identified during alignment quality control after the literature scan; the difference does not affect any headline conclusion (the scoring~$\times$~pathogen interaction is computed identically under both counts because Layer~A appears as a binary label, not a count, in the per-position regression).
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:393:Note that Layer~A selection criteria vary across pathogens: SARS-CoV-2 and H3N2 use phylogenetically confirmed convergent evolution sites, Norovirus uses epochal variant positions, HCV uses hypervariable regions (HVR1/HVR2), and the remaining pathogens use literature-reported immune evasion positions. This heterogeneity is a limitation of the current ground truth construction (discussed in Chapter~\ref{ch:discussion}).
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:396:Six pathogens (SARS-CoV-2, H3N2, HIV-1, RSV, Rabies, EV-A71) have all three layers available.
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:398:These pathogens are nevertheless included because (1)~the primary evaluation metric (MCC) is computed using only Layer~A (positive selection sites as positives, all other positions as negatives), so the core evaluation is valid without Layers~B/C;
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:399:(2)~restricting the benchmark to six pathogens would provide insufficient statistical power for the cross-pathogen analyses (ANOVA, Friedman, LOPO) in Chapter~\ref{ch:results};

chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:439:High H-scores (0.8--1.2) are assigned to Core Candidate Mutation (CCM) seed positions (AA 484, 501, 417, 452---the four Spike positions most frequently mutated in major SARS-CoV-2 variants), moderate scores (0.05--0.3) to surrounding functional regions, and low noise (0.0--0.02) to background positions.

chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:560:Stage~2 systematically evaluates 20 scoring types $\times$ 39 detection parameter variants (from 14 families) $\times$ 11 pathogens = 8,580 combinations to identify the dominant factors influencing hotspot detection performance.
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:602:\multirow{2}{*}{Composite (2)} & EVEscape composite$^{\dagger}$ & EVEscape-style proxy & Multiplicative composite of ESM-2 LLR $\times$ SASA $\times$ Grantham (proxy for fitness $\times$ accessibility $\times$ dissimilarity) \\
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:613:Phylogenetic trees were reconstructed using IQ-TREE 2 with automatic model selection (ModelFinder) and 1,000 ultrafast bootstrap replicates. Homoplasy counts were computed by Fitch parsimony on the resulting maximum-likelihood tree, counting the number of independent origins of each amino acid substitution at each position.
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:628:\textbf{Composite scores} combine multiple information sources: EVEscape integrates evolutionary fitness, structural accessibility, and physicochemical dissimilarity, while EqualWeight provides a naive baseline averaging all normalized scores.
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:629:The \texttt{EVEscape\_composite} channel implements an EVEscape-style multiplicative combination~\cite{thadani2023evescape}: $\text{composite} = \text{ESM-2 LLR}_\text{norm} \times \text{SASA}_\text{norm} \times \text{Grantham}_\text{norm}$, where each component is min-max normalized to $[0, 1]$. This substitutes ESM-2 log-likelihood ratios for the original EVE fitness term, since EVE training is not feasible across all 11 pathogens within the present scope; the structural accessibility (SASA) and physicochemical dissimilarity (Grantham) terms follow the original EVEscape construction.
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:672:Supervised machine learning methods (e.g., Random Forest or gradient boosting classifiers) were not included because they require labeled training data at the position level, and with only 11 pathogens---each having 9--54 Layer~A positives---the available ground truth is insufficient for training generalizable classifiers without severe overfitting.
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:716:Frequency-based thresholding is widely used in viral genomic surveillance; for example, Mercatelli and Giorgi~\cite{mercatelli2020geographic} applied mutation frequency thresholds to identify recurrent SARS-CoV-2 mutations across geographic regions.
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:728:Sliding window approaches are a standard technique in population genetics and genomic analysis; Tajima~\cite{tajima1989statistical} introduced sliding window computation of the D statistic for detecting departures from neutrality, and similar windowed scanning strategies have been widely adopted for identifying regions under selection in viral genomes.
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:740:The 11 pathogens in this benchmark differ in several structural characteristics that are not controlled across pathogens (Table~\ref{tab:design_characteristics}).

chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:769:(1)~subsampling robustness analysis (Section~\ref{sec:robustness_validation}) shows that MCC values stabilize at approximately 1,000 sequences and vary by less than $\pm 0.002$ at 25--100\% subsampling, indicating that sample size is not a dominant driver of performance differences;
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:770:(2)~the key finding is the \emph{scoring $\times$ pathogen interaction} ($\omega^2 = 0.296$), which operates within each pathogen where sample size and positive rate are held constant;
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:784:\item \textbf{MCC (Matthews Correlation Coefficient)}: The primary evaluation metric (defined formally in Equation~\ref{eq:mcc} below).
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:785:The confusion matrix is constructed using only Layer A (positive selection positions) as positive labels: TP = detected positions belonging to Layer A, FP = detected positions not belonging to Layer A, FN = undetected positions belonging to Layer A, TN = undetected positions not belonging to Layer A.
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:786:Layer B (constrained regions) is not included in MCC computation and is evaluated separately via constrained FPR. The majority of genomic positions belonging to neither Layer A nor B are classified as FP or TN depending on detection status.
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:797:Stage~2 uses MCC as the primary metric instead, for three reasons:
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:798:(1)~the stability component of hotspot-score measures bootstrap reproducibility under position-level subsampling, but the subsampling behavior differs fundamentally across pathogens with different alignment lengths (340--1,330 AA) and MSA sizes (530--5,019 unique sequences), making cross-pathogen stability values non-comparable;
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:799:(2)~MCC utilizes all four cells of the confusion matrix (TP, TN, FP, FN), providing a balanced evaluation under the extreme class imbalance inherent in hotspot detection (positive rates 0.7\%--15.9\% across the 11 pathogens);
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:800:and (3)~separating the evaluation metric between stages allows Stage~1 to assess detection \textit{reliability} (via stability) and Stage~2 to assess detection \textit{accuracy} (via MCC), each optimized for its analytical purpose.
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:801:MCC is formally defined as:
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:803:\text{MCC} = \frac{TP \times TN - FP \times FN}{\sqrt{(TP+FP)(TP+FN)(TN+FP)(TN+FN)}}
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:807:MCC ranges from $-1$ (complete disagreement) through $0$ (random prediction) to $+1$ (perfect prediction), and unlike F1, it utilizes all four cells of the confusion matrix, making it robust to class imbalance.
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:808:When any factor in the denominator is zero (e.g., no positive predictions), MCC is conventionally defined as 0.
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:809:MCC was selected as the primary metric because in hotspot detection, where positive positions (convergent evolution sites) constitute a minority of the genome, it provides a more balanced evaluation than F1 for imbalanced classification problems. Chicco and Jurman~\cite{chicco2020mcc} systematically demonstrated that MCC provides more informative evaluation than F1 and accuracy in imbalanced binary classification.
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:810:The stability component used in Stage 1 is excluded from Stage 2 because it is an internal consistency metric independent of external ground truth, and cross-pathogen comparability of Bernoulli masking effects has not been validated given the wide variation in sequence length and MSA size across the 11 pathogens.
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:817:Partial omega-squared ($\omega^2_p$) was computed as the bias-corrected estimate of variance explained. Type~II sum of squares was used because it does not depend on the order of factor entry and provides unbiased estimates when interactions are present. Under Cohen's benchmarks for behavioral sciences~\cite{cohen1988statistical}, $\omega^2 > 0.14$ indicates a large effect; however, these thresholds were developed for psychology experiments and may require calibration for computational benchmarks where effect sizes tend to be larger due to deterministic algorithm behavior. With $N = 8{,}580$, the central limit theorem ensures robustness to non-normality of MCC values.
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:821:No family-wise multiple testing correction (e.g., Bonferroni, Holm) was applied to the ANOVA results because the analysis is exploratory rather than confirmatory: the goal is to decompose variance sources, not to test individual pairwise comparisons. The Friedman test and LOPO cross-validation provide independent confirmation without requiring correction. For the vaccine escape Fisher's exact tests (3 comparisons), significance at $p < 0.01$ (H3N2, HIV-1) exceeds the Bonferroni-corrected threshold of $\alpha/3 = 0.017$.
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:822:Following Cohen's effect size benchmarks~\cite{cohen1988statistical}, $\omega^2$ values are interpreted as small (0.01), medium (0.06), and large ($\geq 0.14$):
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:832:The best-performing combination (scoring $\times$ detection) is selected from $n-1$ of 11 pathogens, applied to the held-out pathogen, and generalization performance is evaluated.
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:833:The best-performing combination is defined as the (scoring, family) pair with the highest mean MCC across the $n-1$ training pathogens.
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:834:Through 11 iterations, the concordance rate between training-best and test-best (oracle) combinations and the performance gap are computed.
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:837:\subsubsection{Friedman Test}
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:839:A nonparametric repeated-measures test using 11 pathogens as blocks, the top $k = 20$ scoring $\times$ family combinations were compared to test whether statistically significant performance differences exist among them.
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:845:Bias-corrected and accelerated (BCa) bootstrap confidence intervals (10,000 resamples) are computed for MCC values across 11 pathogens to quantify the performance variability of the best-performing combination across pathogens. With $n = 11$, the actual coverage of BCa intervals may be somewhat below the nominal 95\% level; these intervals should therefore be interpreted as approximate confidence intervals.
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:849:Random subsamples at 25\%, 50\%, 75\%, and 100\% of MSA sequences are drawn, and the benchmark is repeated to verify MCC stability as a function of sample size.
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:854:Starting from the 10-feature EqualWeight ensemble, each of the 10 scoring types is removed in turn, and the resulting 9-feature ensemble's mean MCC across 11 pathogens is compared to the full 10-feature baseline.
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:855:The change in mean MCC ($\Delta$MCC) quantifies each feature's marginal contribution: negative $\Delta$ indicates that the removed feature improves ensemble performance, while positive $\Delta$ indicates that it introduces noise under uniform weighting.
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:856:Additionally, nested feature subsets of sizes 2, 3, \ldots, 9 are evaluated (selecting features by descending individual AUC) to identify the minimum feature set that captures a target proportion (e.g., 98\%) of full-ensemble performance.
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:873:\textit{Bootstrap confidence intervals}: Region-level bootstrap is performed using the seven functional regions as units.
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:874:In each iteration, seven regions are sampled with replacement to construct a bootstrap ground truth, and the detection results from the full data are re-evaluated against this bootstrap ground truth.
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:883:\textit{Pairwise comparison}: A paired bootstrap design that evaluates two methods simultaneously on the same bootstrap resample, testing the statistical significance of hotspot-score differences between methods.
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:889:(i)~\emph{leave-one-feature-out}: each feature is removed in turn and the change in mean MCC ($\Delta$MCC) is reported;
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:890:(ii)~\emph{group ablation}: features are partitioned into Frequency-only (3), Freq~+~Phylogeny (4), Freq~+~Structure (5), Freq~+~DL (5), and All-10, and group-wise mean MCC is compared;
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:891:(iii)~\emph{cumulative addition}: features are added in descending order of single-feature AUC and the cumulative mean MCC is computed at $k = 1, 2, \ldots, 10$ to identify the minimum subset that recovers a target proportion of the All-10 performance.
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:893:The Stage~3 evaluation set is the same 11 pathogens used in Stage~2, optionally extended to 12 pathogens by adding Zika (E protein, 505~AA) when the analysis benefits from increased per-feature statistical power; the 11-vs-12 distinction is reported transparently in every Stage~3 table caption (Section~\ref{subsec:feature_ablation}).
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:894:A vaccine-escape cross-validation analysis is then performed on the 3 of 11 pathogens with curated antibody-escape annotations (H3N2, SARS-CoV-2, HIV-1; 2{,}340 enrichment evaluations) and audited for circularity against Layer~A (Section~\ref{sec:cross_validation_escape}).
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:898:The full source code, configuration files, scoring scripts, detection-family implementations, ground-truth tables, statistical-analysis notebooks, and the 8{,}580-evaluation result archive are released under an open-source license (see Chapter~\ref{ch:conclusion}, Section~\ref{sec:code_availability} for the canonical repository URL, commit hash, and Zenodo DOI). The pinned random seed (\texttt{seed} = 42) governs all bootstrap, subsampling, and permutation analyses; library versions (Python~3.10, NumPy~1.24, SciPy~1.11, IQ-TREE~2, HyPhy~v2.5, ESM-2 \texttt{esm2\_t33\_650M\_UR50D}, FoldX~5) are pinned in the released environment file.
chapters_en/ch3_methods.tex:903:The following chapter applies this framework to report experimental results: Stage~1 validates the framework on SARS-CoV-2, Stage~2 extends the evaluation to all 11 pathogens to identify the dominant factors influencing hotspot detection performance, and Stage~3 decomposes the resulting performance by information type via per-feature AUC, ablation, and Random Forest analyses.
chapters/ch2_background.tex:25:D614G와 같이 거의 모든 현대 SARS-CoV-2 서열에서 관찰되는 변이는 실제 적응도 이점을 반영하지만, 근고정(near-fixation) 속도는 초기 팬데믹의 창시자 효과에 의해 증폭되어, 빈도 데이터만으로는 선택과 유전적 부동의 상대적 기여를 구분하기 어렵다.
chapters/ch2_background.tex:29:Mullick et al.~\cite{mullick2021entropy}은 Shannon entropy와 K-means clustering을 결합하여 SARS-CoV-2 Spike 단백질의 핫스팟을 탐지하였다.
chapters/ch2_background.tex:36:빈도 기반 변이 분석의 중요한 한계는 \textbf{계통발생학적 비독립성(phylogenetic non-independence)}이다: 근연 서열에서 관찰되는 변이는 독립적 사건이 아니다~\cite{felsenstein1985phylogenies}.
chapters/ch2_background.tex:48:SARS-CoV-2 유전체에 기본 파라미터로 직접 적용하면 데이터의 99.76\%가 단일 거대 클러스터에 병합되며, 수동 조정된 파라미터($\varepsilon = 0.15$, MinPts $= 5$)를 사용하여도 4개의 미분화 클러스터만 얻어져, 생물학적으로 의미 있는 핫스팟 구별이 불가능해진다~\cite{youn2025mutclust}.
chapters/ch2_background.tex:61:SARS-CoV-2의 경우 Starr et al.~\cite{starr2020dms}이 수용체 결합 도메인(RBD)에서 ACE2 결합 친화도와 발현을 측정하였고, Dadonaite et al.~\cite{dadonaite2023dms}이 전체 길이 Spike 단백질에서 슈도바이러스 세포 진입 적응도를 측정하였다.
chapters/ch2_background.tex:62:Bloom and Neher~\cite{bloom2023fitness}는 모든 SARS-CoV-2 단백질에 걸친 DMS 적응도 효과의 통합 분석을 제공하였다.
chapters/ch2_background.tex:70:(1)~ProteinGym~\cite{notin2023proteingym}은 250개 이상의 DMS 분석을 활용하여 변이 효과 예측 모델을 벤치마킹하나, 이는 잔기별 회귀 과제로서 핫스팟 영역 탐지와는 근본적으로 다른 문제이다;
chapters/ch2_background.tex:73:(4)~개별 SARS-CoV-2 핫스팟 연구들~\cite{harvey2021tracking}은 엔트로피나 클러스터링을 사용하여 소수의 알려진 변이주와 검증하나, 표준화된 ground truth나 교차 방법 비교가 없다.
chapters/ch2_background.tex:97:핵심 파라미터($\gamma=10$, $d=3$, MinPts$=5$)는 224,318개 SARS-CoV-2 서열로부터 경험적으로 결정되었으며, 전체 시간 복잡도는 $O(N + M \log M)$으로 $N$은 유전체 길이, $M$은 변이 위치 수이다.
chapters/ch2_background.tex:99:\subsection{SARS-CoV-2 핫스팟 탐지 결과}
chapters/ch2_background.tex:102:224,318개 GISAID SARS-CoV-2 서열을 우한-Hu-1 참조 유전체(NC\_045512.2, 29,903 bp)에 정렬하여 분석한 결과, MutClust는 \textbf{477개}의 변이 핫스팟을 탐지하였으며, 이는 DBSCAN으로 얻은 4개 클러스터와 질적으로 완전히 다른 수준의 해상도이다.
chapters/ch2_background.tex:104:인플루엔자에 대한 검증(276,910개 서열, 3개 아형)에서도 D222G(H1N1), E627K(H3N2), K338R(B-Victoria) 등 임상적으로 중요한 변이가 핫스팟으로 성공적으로 탐지되어 일반화 가능성이 확인되었다.
chapters/ch2_background.tex:105:특히 H3N2의 경우, Smith et al.~\cite{smith2004antigenic}이 항원 지도작성(antigenic cartography)을 통해 HA 단백질의 소수 치환이 항원 변화를 주도함을 밝힌 바 있어, 이러한 핵심 위치의 정확한 탐지가 중요하다.
chapters/ch2_background.tex:106:그러나 인플루엔자 유전체는 SARS-CoV-2의 약 10분의 1 크기이므로, 최적 성능을 위해서는 유전체 특성에 맞춘 파라미터 재조정이 필요할 수 있다.
chapters/ch2_background.tex:117:$\gamma=10$, $d=3$, CCM 임계값(0.03, 0.01, 0.05)은 224,318개 SARS-CoV-2 서열에 맞춰 경험적으로 설정된 값이다.
chapters/ch2_background.tex:119:인플루엔자 검증에서 동일 파라미터의 적용이 성공적이었지만, 인플루엔자 유전체는 SARS-CoV-2의 약 10분의 1 크기($\sim$2,300 bp/분절 대 $\sim$30,000 bp)이므로 최적 성능을 위한 파라미터 재조정의 필요성이 불확실한 채로 남아 있다.
chapters/ch2_background.tex:124:MutClust를 포함한 바이러스 핫스팟 탐지 방법들은 자기 참조적 통계 검정(bootstrap)에만 의존하며, 표준화된 평가 지표의 부재로 인해 서로 다른 방법의 결과를 공정하게 비교하는 것이 불가능하다.

front/abstract_kr.tex:14:Stage~1에서는 MutClust-Hybrid가 최고 hotspot-score(0.778)를 달성하여,
front/abstract_kr.tex:16:Stage~2의 핵심 발견은 최적의 생물학적 정보원이 병원체마다 체계적으로 다르다는 것이다: 점수화 방법과 병원체 간 상호작용이 모델된 변량 중 가장 큰 성분($\omega^2_{\text{scoring} \times \text{pathogen}} = 0.296$, 20-type 기준; 95\% 클러스터 부트스트랩 CI [0.195, 0.333]; 셀 내부 잔차 $\omega^2 \approx 0.39$는 미모델 성분; 6-카테고리 집계 시 $\omega^2 = 0.103$을 공선성 보정 하한으로 제공)이다.
front/abstract_kr.tex:17:Friedman 검정($\chi^2 = 7.69$, $p = 0.990$)은 보편적으로 우월한 단일 조합이 존재하지 않음을 나타내며, LOPO 교차검증에서 0/11 정확 일치와 oracle-vs-generalized 평균 MCC 격차 0.265가 관찰되어 병원체 정체성을 무시할 때 상당한 성능 손실이 있음을 시사한다(단 0/11 자체는 780조합 무작위 null에서도 $P{\approx}0.96$로 기대되므로, 증거는 $\omega^2$ 상호작용과 HIV-1 외부 검증의 결합으로 해석되어야 한다).
front/abstract_kr.tex:19:실용적 검증 측면에서, 병원체 최적화된 단일 scoring이 HIV-1에 대해 7.19배 백신 escape enrichment(Bonferroni 보정 $p = 2.5 \times 10^{-16}$; escape 집합의 82\%가 Layer~A와 disjoint)를 달성하여 가장 정직한 외부 검증 근거로 기능한다. 헤드라인 H3N2 9.36배는 69\% Layer~A 중복으로 self-consistency 검증에 가깝고(novel-only 시 7.19배, Fisher $p=0.132$ 비유의), SARS-CoV-2 7.63배는 Bonferroni 보정 후 유의성이 소실되어 탐색적 결과로 분류된다. 백신-escape 검증은 3개 병원체(2{,}340회 평가)로 제한되며, 이는 주석 데이터 가용성에 의한 것이다.
front/abstract_kr.tex:21:6개 정보 카테고리(빈도 기반, MSA 유래, 계통 분석, 구조 기반, AI 기반, 복합)에 걸친 20개 점수화 유형 분석에서 11개 병원체에 걸쳐 9가지 서로 다른 최적 정보 유형이 관찰되었다: FUBAR 계통선택 점수(H3N2), 호모플래시(Norovirus), 단백질 언어모델(SARS-CoV-2, RSV), 의미적 변화(EV-A71), 안정성 예측(Rabies), 빈도 기반(HCV, Influenza B, MERS).
front/abstract_kr.tex:22:다중 정보 통합이 실험적 탐색 범위를 축소하며(H3N2 백신 escape enrichment 4.012배, $p = 0.0023$), 4개 핵심 특징(homoplasy, pLDDT, entropy, frequency)이 전체 앙상블 성능의 98\%를 달성하였다.

review/2026-04-17/phase_ch3_cycle12.md:11:### CR-Ch3-1 — Layer A operational definition is **not pathogen-uniform** and is largely literature-curated rather than algorithmic
review/2026-04-17/phase_ch3_cycle12.md:13:- **Issue**: Layer A is defined as "≥3 phylogenetically distinct lineages with recurrent nonsynonymous mutation" (L 297), but L 300 explicitly states *"No computational tool was applied to identify new convergent evolution positions; all positions were taken directly from the cited literature."* L 368 then admits: *"Layer A selection criteria vary across pathogens: SARS-CoV-2/H3N2 use phylogenetically confirmed convergent evolution sites, Norovirus uses epochal variant positions, HCV uses hypervariable regions (HVR1/HVR2), and the remaining pathogens use literature-reported immune evasion positions."* This is a **heterogeneous composite ground truth**, not the "entropy quantile" Layer A described in the task brief.
review/2026-04-17/phase_ch3_cycle12.md:14:- **Why Critical**: The dissertation's headline finding (ω²=0.296 scoring × pathogen interaction) is computed against MCC where TP=Layer A. If Layer A definition itself varies by pathogen (convergent vs hypervariable region vs literature immune-escape), then part of the "scoring × pathogen interaction" may be a *Layer-A-definition × scoring* interaction. This is not reproducible from the chapter alone — a reader cannot regenerate Layer A for a new pathogen.
review/2026-04-17/phase_ch3_cycle12.md:19:- **Issue**: L 792: *"The three-way interaction was not estimated due to insufficient within-cell replication."* But 8,580 / (20×14×11) = 2.78 observations per cell on average — this *is* the within-cell n, and it is not stated. The chapter doesn't show whether cells are balanced (some scoring × family combinations have only 1 detector parameter variant).
review/2026-04-17/phase_ch3_cycle12.md:25:- **Issue**: No DOI / repository URL / Zenodo / GitHub link for MutBench code. No random seeds for: BCa bootstrap (L 821, 10,000 resamples), permutation tests (L 854, 1,000 perms), bootstrap stability subsampling (L 491, 100 iterations), LOPO (L 808–811), subsample robustness (L 825). review/2026-04-17/phase_ch3_cycle12.md:107:Ch3 Methods has comprehensive prose coverage of materials (11 pathogens, L 21–162) and a clean three-component pipeline figure (L 175–217), but the chapter has **three reproducibility-blocking Critical issues**: Layer A is literature-curated with pathogen-heterogeneous criteria (L 297–300, 368) rather than algorithmically defined; the three-way ANOVA omits the highest interaction with no within-cell n disclosure (L 792); and there is **no code repository, dataset snapshot, or random seed disclosure anywhere in the chapter**. Together these mean a reader cannot regenerate either the ground truth or the headline ω²=0.296 result. Major issues center on incomplete formal specification: MutClust's γ parameter is undefined (L 473), five Stage 1 variants (v1–v3) have no HDBSCAN hyperparameters (L 475), 12 of 20 scoring types lack explicit formulas (L 540–604, corroborated by Phase 0 CHECK 5c WARNs), DBSCAN min_samples is omitted (L 670), Bayesian detector likelihood is unstated (L 672), and no power analysis exists for n=11 LOPO/Friedman/BCa (L 806–821). The C11 known issues recur in Ch3: ViroGym/EVEREST/AlphaMissense/DCA receive zero mentions (Grep confirms), so the methods chapter does not position MutBench's design choices against the only direct competitor benchmark. Stage 3 (vaccine escape integration) has no methods section despite extensive Stage 3 figures and a Ch5 adapt chapter — Ch3 declares only a "two-stage design" (L 7). Minor issues are mostly cosmetic or arithmetic transparency. Recommended priorities: (1) Add code/data availability subsection with seeds; (2) consolidate or appendix-ize Layer A position lists with per-pathogen citation; (3) add a Stage 3 methods subsection bridging to Ch5 adapt; (4) cite ViroGym in design rationale; (5) restate γ, HDBSCAN params, DBSCAN min_samples explicitly.

chapters/ch1_introduction.tex:8:2019년 말 출현한 SARS-CoV-2는 전 세계적으로 7억 건 이상의 확진 사례를 발생시키며, 바이러스 유전체 분석의 중요성을 재확인시켰다~\cite{harvey2021tracking}.
chapters/ch1_introduction.tex:26:MutClust의 유일한 검증 수단인 bootstrap 검정은 검출된 클러스터의 통계적 유의성만을 확인하는 자기 참조적 방법으로, 해당 클러스터가 생물학적으로 의미 있는 기능적 영역에 대응하는지는 검증할 수 없다.
chapters/ch1_introduction.tex:44:  \item \textbf{바이러스 변이 hotspot 검출을 위한 체계적 벤치마크 프레임워크(MutBench)의 구축}: 3계층 ground truth(수렴 진화 기반 양성, 정제 선택 기반 음성, DMS 기능적 적합도), hotspot-score $= (\text{recall} + \text{precision} + \text{stability}) / 3$ (여기서 stability는 부분추출 반복 시 탐지 결과의 재현성을 측정한다) 복합 평가 지표, 2단계 실험 설계(1단계: SARS-CoV-2 심층 분석, 2단계: 9종 RNA 바이러스 $\times$ 9가지 스코어링 $\times$ 39개 탐지 방법, 총 3,159개 평가)를 포함하는 벤치마크 프레임워크를 구축한다.
chapters/ch1_introduction.tex:46:  \item \textbf{병원체 적응적 방법 선택의 필요성에 대한 경험적 입증}: 대규모 벤치마크 결과에 대한 통계 분석(ANOVA, Friedman 검정, LOPO 교차 검증)을 통해, 단일 최적 방법이라는 전제가 병원체 전반에 걸쳐 성립하지 않음을 경험적으로 확립하고, PAHD 프레임워크의 개념 증명 프로토타입을 제시한다(제~\ref{ch:results}장 참조).
chapters/ch1_introduction.tex:58:정확도(recall, precision)와 신뢰성(stability)을 동시에 평가하는 hotspot-score 복합 지표를 도입하고, SARS-CoV-2 심층 분석과 9종 병원체 대규모 비교를 결합하는 2단계 실험 설계를 제시하였다.
chapters/ch1_introduction.tex:61:9종 RNA 바이러스에 대한 평가 결과, 9개 병원체 모두 상이한 최적 조합을 보이며(LOPO 교차 검증 0/9 일치), 방법 계열과 병원체 간 상호작용이 ANOVA에서 최대 분산 원천이었다.
chapters/ch1_introduction.tex:62:Friedman 검정은 방법 간 성능 순위가 병원체에 따라 체계적으로 달라짐을 확인하였다.
chapters/ch1_introduction.tex:76:\textbf{제~\ref{ch:results}장, 실험 결과}에서는 실험 결과를 네 개 절로 구분하여 보고한다: 단일 병원체 벤치마크(합성 데이터 비교, 다중 ground truth 평가, 실제 GISAID 검증, SARS-CoV-2에 대한 외부 방법 비교), 견고성 검증(통계적 검증, 민감도 분석, 시간적 일반화, indel 제외), 교차 병원체 검증(H3N2 검증, 3D 구조 분석, 계통발생학적 시뮬레이션, ESM-2 교차 패러다임 검증), 9-병원체 대규모 벤치마크(ANOVA, Friedman 검정, LOPO 교차 검증, PAHD 개념 증명 프로토타입).

chapters/ch3_methods.tex:6:전체 파이프라인은 9종 RNA 바이러스의 다중서열정렬(MSA) 데이터를 9가지 스코어링 공식과 39개 탐지 방법으로 처리하고, 3계층 ground truth 체계에 대해 hotspot-score 복합 지표와 Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC)로 평가한다.
chapters/ch3_methods.tex:7:평가는 2단계 구조를 따른다: 1단계는 SARS-CoV-2에 대한 깊이 우선 분석으로 프레임워크 구성요소를 검증하고, 2단계는 9종 병원체 전체로 확장하여 대규모 교차 병원체 비교를 수행한다.
chapters/ch3_methods.tex:19:(1)~\textit{호흡기 바이러스}: SARS-CoV-2 (Spike, 1,273 AA), MERS-CoV (Spike, 1,330 AA), RSV (F protein, 574 AA), Influenza A H3N2 (HA, 566 AA), Influenza B (HA, 584 AA);
chapters/ch3_methods.tex:20:(2)~\textit{혈액 매개/성 매개}: HIV-1 (Env gp120, 480 AA), HCV (E2, 340 AA);
chapters/ch3_methods.tex:23:이 9종 병원체는 $\sim$10$^{-3}$ (HIV-1)에서 $\sim$10$^{-4}$ (SARS-CoV-2) substitutions/site/year에 이르는 돌연변이율, 340--1,330 AA의 정렬 길이, 급속 항원 표류(H3N2)에서 에포칼 진화(Norovirus)에 이르는 진화 패턴을 아우른다.
chapters/ch3_methods.tex:25:각 병원체의 FASTA 서열은 NCBI GenBank에서 각 표적 단백질명(예: ``SARS-CoV-2 spike glycoprotein'')으로 조회하여 수집하였으며, 완전 코딩 서열 필터를 적용하고 부분 서열 및 실험실 유래 구조물은 제외하였다. 날짜 범위 제한은 적용하지 않았으며, 2024년 12월 기준 이용 가능한 모든 서열을 다운로드하였다. 모호 염기(N)가 5\% 초과인 서열은 제거하고, 동일 서열은 중복 제거하였다(표~\ref{tab:pathogen_data}의 ``고유 서열 수'' 열은 중복 제거 후 수치이다). 각 표면 단백질(SARS-CoV-2: Spike, H3N2: HA, HIV-1: Env gp120 등)에 대해 MAFFT v7.505~\cite{katoh2013mafft}의 \texttt{--auto} 모드로 다중서열정렬(MSA)을 수행한 후 위치별 변이 빈도와 엔트로피를 산출하였다.

chapters/ch3_methods.tex:68:\subsubsection{Layer A: 적응적 양성 선택 (Adaptive)}
chapters/ch3_methods.tex:71:예를 들어, SARS-CoV-2 Spike 단백질 484번 위치의 변이---항체 결합 표면을 변화시킴으로써 면역 회피를 가능하게 하는 변이---는 Beta, Gamma, Mu 계통에서 E484K(글루탐산→라이신)로, Omicron 계통에서 E484A(글루탐산→알라닌)로 각각 독립적으로 출현하였으며, 이 계통들은 SARS-CoV-2 계통수의 서로 다른 조상 분지로부터 유래하였다. 동일 위치에서의 이러한 반복적 독립 출현은 해당 부위에 대한 양성 선택의 강력한 근거를 제공한다.
chapters/ch3_methods.tex:78:예를 들어, SARS-CoV-2 Layer~A 위치(예: E484, N501, L452, K417)는 Carabelli 등~\cite{carabelli2023convergent}이 Alpha, Beta, Gamma, Delta, Omicron 계통에서의 독립적 출현을 계통발생 분석으로 확인하여 식별하였다.
chapters/ch3_methods.tex:91:SARS-CoV-2의 경우, 154개 Layer~B 위치에는 HR1 (AA 912--984) 및 HR2 (AA 1,163--1,213) 헵타드 반복과 구조적 시스테인 잔기가 포함되며, cryo-EM 구조~\cite{wrapp2020cryo} 및 보존 분석으로부터 식별되었다.
chapters/ch3_methods.tex:96:심층 돌연변이 스캐닝(Deep Mutational Scanning) 실험 데이터가 이용 가능한 4종의 병원체---SARS-CoV-2~\cite{dadonaite2023dms}, HIV-1, H3N2, RSV---에 대해 실험적으로 측정된 fitness 효과를 ground truth로 사용한다.
chapters/ch3_methods.tex:97:DMS 실험에서는 모든 가능한 단일 아미노산 치환을 실험실에서 물리적으로 만들어, 정량적 표현형(예: SARS-CoV-2의 세포 진입 효율, H3N2의 복제 적합도)에 미치는 영향을 측정한다. 이 층은 진화 데이터에서 아직 보이지 않는 기능적 중요성을 포착할 수 있다.
chapters/ch3_methods.tex:100:\textbf{Layer A/B 중복 처리.}
chapters/ch3_methods.tex:101:RSV(positions 148, 152)와 Influenza B(positions 141, 194)에서 Layer A와 Layer B가 중복되는 위치가 존재한다.
chapters/ch3_methods.tex:103:MCC 평가에서 이 위치들은 Layer A(양성)로 우선 분류하며, Layer B(음성) 집합에서는 제외한다.

chapters/ch3_methods.tex:132:\footnotesize Layer C (DMS) 출처: SARS-CoV-2~\cite{dadonaite2023dms}, H3N2~\cite{lee2018h3n2dms}, HIV-1~\cite{haddox2018hiv1dms}, RSV~\cite{simonich2026rsvdms}.
chapters/ch3_methods.tex:136:Layer~A 선정 기준은 병원체별로 상이하다: SARS-CoV-2와 H3N2는 계통발생적으로 확인된 수렴 진화 부위, Norovirus는 epochal variant 위치, HCV는 초가변 영역(HVR1/HVR2), 나머지 병원체는 문헌 보고 면역 회피 위치를 사용한다. 이 이질성은 현재 ground truth 구성의 한계이다(제~\ref{ch:discussion}장에서 논의).
chapters/ch3_methods.tex:161:모든 분석은 SARS-CoV-2 참조 게놈(Wuhan-Hu-1, GenBank: NC\_045512.2)을 사용하며, Spike 유전자는 뉴클레오티드 위치 21,563--25,384에 위치한다.

chapters/ch3_methods.tex:592:\item \textbf{MCC (Matthews Correlation Coefficient)}: 주요 평가 지표(식~\ref{eq:mcc}에 공식 정의).
chapters/ch3_methods.tex:593:혼동행렬은 Layer A(양성 선택 위치)만을 양성 레이블로 사용하여 구성된다: TP = 탐지되었으며 Layer A에 속하는 위치, FP = 탐지되었으나 Layer A에 속하지 않는 위치, FN = 탐지되지 않았으나 Layer A에 속하는 위치, TN = 탐지되지 않았으며 Layer A에도 속하지 않는 위치.
chapters/ch3_methods.tex:594:Layer B(구속 영역)는 MCC 계산에 포함되지 않으며 별도의 constrained FPR로 평가된다. Layer A에도 B에도 속하지 않는 다수의 게놈 위치는 탐지 여부에 따라 FP 또는 TN으로 분류된다.
chapters/ch3_methods.tex:603:Stage~1에서는 안정성을 포함하는 hotspot-score를 사용하여 단일 병원체 심층 분석을 수행하지만, Stage~2에서는 안정성의 교차 병원체 비교 가능성이 검증되지 않았고 MCC가 극단적 클래스 불균형에 더 적합하므로 MCC를 주 평가 지표로 채택한다.
chapters/ch3_methods.tex:606:둘째, MCC는 혼동행렬의 네 셀(TP, TN, FP, FN) 모두를 활용하여, 핫스팟 탐지에 내재하는 극단적 클래스 불균형(9종 병원체의 양성률 1--16\%) 하에서 균형 잡힌 평가를 제공한다.
chapters/ch3_methods.tex:607:셋째, 단계 간 평가 지표를 분리함으로써 1단계에서는 탐지의 \textit{신뢰성}(안정성)을, 2단계에서는 탐지의 \textit{정확성}(MCC)을 각 분석 목적에 맞게 평가할 수 있다.
chapters/ch3_methods.tex:608:MCC는 다음과 같이 정의된다:
chapters/ch3_methods.tex:610:\text{MCC} = \frac{TP \times TN - FP \times FN}{\sqrt{(TP+FP)(TP+FN)(TN+FP)(TN+FN)}}
chapters/ch3_methods.tex:614:MCC는 $-1$(완전 불일치)에서 $0$(무작위 예측)을 거쳐 $+1$(완전 예측)의 범위이며, F1과 달리 혼동행렬의 네 셀 모두를 활용하므로 클래스 불균형에 강건하다.
chapters/ch3_methods.tex:615:분모의 어떤 인수가 0일 때(예: 양성 예측 없음), MCC는 관례적으로 0으로 정의한다.
chapters/ch3_methods.tex:616:MCC를 주요 지표로 선택한 이유는, 핫스팟 탐지에서 양성 위치(수렴 진화 부위)가 전체 게놈의 소수를 차지하는 불균형 분류 문제에서 F1보다 균형 잡힌 평가를 제공하기 때문이다. Chicco and Jurman~\cite{chicco2020mcc}은 불균형 이진 분류에서 MCC가 F1 및 정확도보다 유의미한 평가를 제공함을 체계적으로 입증하였다.
chapters/ch3_methods.tex:625:효과 크기로 편향 보정된 $\omega^2$ (omega-squared)를 사용하며, 이는 $\eta^2$가 표본 크기에 따라 상향 편향되는 문제를 회피한다. $\omega^2$ 값은 Cohen의 효과 크기 기준~\cite{cohen1988statistical}에 따라 0.01(소), 0.06(중), 0.14 이상(대)으로 해석된다:
chapters/ch3_methods.tex:635:9회 반복하여 훈련 최적 조합과 테스트 최적 조합(oracle)의 일치율 및 성능 격차를 산출한다.
chapters/ch3_methods.tex:637:\subsubsection{Friedman 검정}
chapters/ch3_methods.tex:643:9개 병원체의 MCC 값에 대해 편향 보정 가속(BCa, bias-corrected and accelerated) 부트스트랩 신뢰 구간을 산출하여, 최적 조합의 병원체 간 성능 변동성을 정량화한다.
chapters/ch3_methods.tex:647:MSA 서열의 25\%, 50\%, 75\%, 100\% 비율로 무작위 하위표본을 추출하여 벤치마크를 반복 수행하고, 표본 크기에 따른 MCC 안정성을 검증한다.
chapters/ch3_methods.tex:664:\textbf{부트스트랩 신뢰 구간}: 7개 기능 영역을 단위로 한 영역 수준 부트스트랩(region-level bootstrap)을 수행한다.
chapters/ch3_methods.tex:674:\textbf{쌍별 비교}: 동일 부트스트랩 리샘플에서 두 방법을 동시에 평가하는 paired bootstrap 설계로, 방법 간 hotspot-score 차이의 통계적 유의성을 검정한다.

chapters/ch5_discussion.tex:13:\label{sec:bootstrap_interpretation}
chapters/ch5_discussion.tex:26:밀도 기반 클러스터링은 이러한 극단적 희소 분포에서 클러스터 형성이 제한되며(HDBSCAN-Auto는 클러스터 미형성), 합성 벤치마크에서의 MutClust-Hybrid 대비 우위(hotspot-score 0.778 vs. 0.646)도 희소 분포에서는 사라져 두 방법의 성능이 수렴한다(0.383 vs. 0.386).
chapters/ch5_discussion.tex:28:그럼에도, 실제 GISAID 데이터에서도 농축비가 무작위 기준선 대비 6.9--8.0배를 유지하여, 상위 방법이 포착하는 생물학적 신호는 MCC/F1의 실질적 하락에도 불구하고 보존됨을 보여준다.
chapters/ch5_discussion.tex:49:시간적 검증(제~\ref{sec:temporal}절)에서 관찰된 H-score 포화 현상은 참조 기반 지표의 근본적 한계를 드러낸다: 2024--2025 데이터에서 모든 1,273개 Spike 위치가 비영 H-score를 가지며 표준 편차는 0.098에 불과하여 판별력을 상실한다.
chapters/ch5_discussion.tex:61:SARS-CoV-2 내에서 관찰된 ground truth 의존적 방법 순위는 9-병원체 벤치마크에서 드러난 병원체 의존적 순위를 예고한다.
chapters/ch5_discussion.tex:72:예를 들어, 전체적으로 높은 변이율을 가진 병원체(예: H3N2, 모든 위치가 비영 H-score)는 역치 기반 시드 탐지의 이점을 무력화하는 반면, 컴팩트한 게놈과 소수의 수렴 진화 부위를 가진 병원체(예: MERS)는 희소 데이터에서 약한 신호를 탐지할 수 있는 방법을 선호한다.
chapters/ch5_discussion.tex:75:구체적으로, MutBench의 결과는 Rice 프레임워크를 다음과 같이 실체화한다: \textit{문제 공간} $\mathcal{P}$는 게노믹 프로파일(정렬 길이, 다양성 비율, ground truth 밀도 등)로 특성화된 병원체로 구성되고, \textit{알고리즘 공간} $\mathcal{A}$는 351개의 scoring--detection 조합(9 $\times$ 39)으로 구성되며, \textit{성능 공간} $\mathcal{Y}$는 3-layer ground truth에 대해 평가된 MCC이다. 상호작용 우세($\omega^2 = 0.285$)는 매핑 $f: \mathcal{P} \to \mathcal{A}$가 비자명함을 실증적으로 확인하며, 이는 어떤 단일 알고리즘도 모든 가능한 문제 분포에서 다른 모든 알고리즘을 능가할 수 없다는 No Free Lunch 정리~\cite{wolpert1997nfl}의 직관과 일치하는 발견이다. PAHD 프로토타입의 9개 중 5개 양의 MCC 결과는 프로파일 공간 $\mathcal{P}$에서 단순한 최근접 이웃 접근법만으로도 이 매핑을 부분적으로 복원할 수 있음을 보여주며, 더 정교한 메타 학습 접근법의 동기를 제공한다.
chapters/ch5_discussion.tex:77:PAHD 프로토타입 결과(제~\ref{subsec:pahd_prototype}절)는 더 거친 예측 단위에서 oracle 성능의 최대 57.7\%를 회복할 수 있음을 보여주나, $n = 9$의 한계는 여전히 존재한다.
chapters/ch5_discussion.tex:78:ESM-2 교차 패러다임 검증(제~\ref{subsec:esm_validation}절)은 이 발견을 더욱 강화한다: ESM-LLR은 SARS-CoV-2와 MERS에서 1위를 차지하였으나 Norovirus와 HIV-1에서는 최하위를 기록하여, MSA 기반이든 단백질 언어 모델 기반이든 어떤 단일 스코어링 패러다임도 모든 병원체에서 우위를 점하지 못함을 확인하였다.
chapters/ch5_discussion.tex:84:\label{sec:oracle_mcc_ceiling}
chapters/ch5_discussion.tex:86:9개 병원체에 걸친 평균 oracle MCC는 0.298(범위: 0.088--0.549)이며, 이 값이 낮아 보일 수 있으나 세 가지 구조적 요인으로 설명된다.
chapters/ch5_discussion.tex:88:둘째, \textbf{극단적 클래스 불균형}(양성 비율 대부분 10\% 미만)이 달성 가능한 MCC를 제약한다---양성 비율 5\%에서 90\% 재현율과 30\% 정밀도는 이론적 MCC 0.49만을 산출한다.
chapters/ch5_discussion.tex:91:이러한 제약에도 불구하고, oracle MCC 0.298은 명백히 비무작위이다: 무작위 기준선(10,000회 순열)의 평균은 0.001(SD = 0.003)이며, oracle은 무작위 기대보다 약 99 표준편차 위에 위치한다.
chapters/ch5_discussion.tex:93:따라서 oracle MCC 0.298은 위치 수준 생물학적 예측 과제의 본질적 난이도와 일치한다.
chapters/ch5_discussion.tex:97:$\pm5$ 윈도우는 대략 단일 단백질 이차 구조 요소 또는 항원 에피토프({$\sim$}15개 잔기)에 해당하여 생물학적으로 의미 있는 근접성 기준을 제공한다. 이 분석은 위치 정확 평가의 엄격성에 대한 민감도 검사로 기능하며, 대체가 아니다: 위치 정확 MCC는 매개변수가 없고 완전한 재현성을 보장하므로 주요 지표로 유지된다.
chapters/ch5_discussion.tex:98:$\pm10$ 윈도우 평가에서 평균 oracle MCC는 0.289에서 0.712로 146\% 향상되었다.
chapters/ch5_discussion.tex:99:특히 H3N2는 $\pm10$에서 MCC = 0.964(정확 매칭 0.521 대비)를 달성하여, 탐지된 핫스팟이 정확히 중첩되지 않더라도 알려진 항원 변이 부위에 공간적으로 근접함을 확인하였다.

chapters/ch5_discussion.tex:126:{\footnotesize $^\dagger$영역 중첩 분석의 위치 정확 MCC(0.289)는 벤치마크 보고 oracle(0.298)과 약간 차이가 나는데, 이는 영역 중첩 분석이 경계 처리(예: 정렬 경계의 가장자리 위치 처리)에서 소규모 차이가 있는 재구현된 평가 파이프라인을 사용하기 때문이다. 절대적 기준선 차이(0.009, 즉 3.1\%)는 주요 발견에 영향을 미치지 않는다: 위치 정확에서 영역 중첩으로의 상대적 향상(146\%)은 탐지된 핫스팟이 ground truth 위치에 공간적으로 근접함을 보여준다.}

chapters/ch5_discussion.tex:142:제~\ref{ch:introduction}장에서 제기한 세 가지 문제로 돌아가면: 표준화된 평가 프레임워크의 부재는 MutBench의 3계층 ground truth와 hotspot-score 지표로 해결되었으며(기여 1); 교차 병원체 일반화 근거의 부족은 네 가지 독립적인 통계적 증거에 의해 해소되었고(기여 2); 탐지 방법의 병원체 의존성은 ANOVA 상호작용 우세($\omega^2 = 0.285$)와 LOPO 실패(0/9)로 정량화되어, PAHD 프레임워크의 동기를 제공하였다.
chapters/ch5_discussion.tex:148:SARS-CoV-2의 세대 시간(약 5일)과 서열 제출 지연(중앙값 약 14일)을 감안하면, 실시간 TC-freq 경보에는 최소 4주 윈도우가 필요하다.
chapters/ch5_discussion.tex:163:MutClust-Hybrid (단독) & 0.968 & 0.659 & 0.785 & 852 & 0.706 & 0.778 \\
chapters/ch5_discussion.tex:178:본 연구의 모든 탐지 방법은 서열 간 독립성을 암묵적으로 가정하나, SARS-CoV-2 서열은 계통발생적으로 구조화되어 있어 빈도 기반 접근법만으로는 양성 선택과 founder effect를 구분할 수 없다(예: D614G;~\cite{korber2020tracking}).
chapters/ch5_discussion.tex:199:표본 크기($n=9$)의 제한에도 불구하고, Friedman 검정은 $p=0.0015$를 달성하여, 효과 크기가 제한된 수의 병원체로도 탐지 가능할 만큼 충분히 크다는 것을 보여준다.
chapters/ch5_discussion.tex:205:ESM-2~\cite{lin2023esm2}는 바이러스 단백질 서열을 포함하는 UniRef50/UniRef90으로 학습되었으며, 본 벤치마크의 9개 대상 단백질(예: SARS-CoV-2 Spike, HIV-1 gp120, H3N2 HA)은 학습 코퍼스에 포함되어 있을 가능성이 높다.
chapters/ch5_discussion.tex:216:SARS-CoV-2와 H3N2의 경우, Layer~A 위치는 계통발생적으로 확인된 수렴 진화 부위---동일한 돌연변이가 독립적으로 여러 계통에서 발생한 위치---이다.
chapters/ch5_discussion.tex:218:이러한 이질성은 ANOVA에서 방법 $\times$ 병원체 상호작용을 인위적으로 부풀릴 수 있다. 병원체 생물학의 차이뿐만 아니라 ground truth 정의 기준의 차이도 관찰된 상호작용 효과($\omega^2 = 0.285$)에 기여할 수 있기 때문이다.

review/2026-04-17/phase2_redteam_cycle2.md:17:**[Critical] ch4:394 — 주장: "Three complementary analyses of the same 8,580-evaluation dataset yield consistent interpretations" — 공격: 이 문장은 "same 8,580-evaluation dataset"임을 명시하며 "their agreement is consistency rather than independent replication"을 추가했지만, 여전히 ANOVA($\omega^2 = 0.296$), Friedman($p = 0.990$), LOPO(0/11)를 "(1)(2)(3)"으로 병렬 열거하며 "jointly they support the interpretation that the optimal information source is pathogen-dependent"로 종결한다. 세 분석은 동일 CSV(3321 rows, 2544 rows)에서 파생된 **동일 통계량의 재표현**이다: ANOVA interaction은 pathogen별 best combo 차이를 variance 형태로, Friedman은 동일 차이를 rank 형태로, LOPO는 동일 차이를 prediction error 형태로 측정한다. "consistent interpretations"이라는 표현은 **동일 현상의 세 측정이 일치한다**는 tautology를 "세 독립 증거의 수렴"으로 과대 포장하는 수사이다. 진정한 수렴이라면 최소한 서로 다른 데이터(예: external benchmark, independent pathogen set, 다른 ground truth layer)에서의 일치가 있어야 한다. 이는 cycle 1에서 Critical로 지적된 "Three analyses converge"의 **언어적 교정에만 머물고 논리적 결함은 해소하지 못한 상태**이다. — 치명도 근거: Contribution 2의 "strong statistical evidence"(ch1:148)가 "independent confirmations"에 의해 뒷받침되는 것으로 독자에게 읽히며, 실제로는 모델 재매개화(re-parameterization)에 불과하다.
review/2026-04-17/phase2_redteam_cycle2.md:19:**[Critical] ch4:814, ch4:794 — 주장: "For H3N2, FUBAR Bayes factor captures 9 of 29 antigenic drift sites with 9.36-fold enrichment, substantially outperforming frequency-based approaches" + Table 2.vaccine_escape_stage3에 $p < 0.0001$ 표기 — 공격: Table caption(ch4:786)에는 Bonferroni 해설이 추가되어 "SARS-CoV-2 nominal $p = 0.026$ does not survive"만 인정하지만, "H3N2 and HIV-1 require the exact $p$ value … to determine Bonferroni survival---the supplementary enrichment CSV reports these exact values"로 **판정을 외부 CSV에 떠넘긴다**. 본문(ch4:814)은 여전히 "9.36-fold enrichment"를 무조건적으로 주장하고, Abstract(abstract:12)도 "up to 9.36-fold enrichment for experimentally confirmed vaccine escape positions"를 "$p < 0.0001$, uncorrected"로 약화시켰지만, Ch6:27은 "(H3N2: 9.36× via single FUBAR scoring, HIV-1: 7.19×; both $p < 0.0001$, uncorrected)"로 "uncorrected" 한 단어를 추가하며 정량적 보정 결과를 제시하지 않는다. Bonferroni factor는 780이므로 $p_{\text{adj}} = \min(1, 780 \cdot p)$; $p_{\text{nominal}} < 10^{-4}$라도 $p_{\text{adj}} < 0.078$이 되려면 $p_{\text{nominal}} < 10^{-4}/780 \approx 1.3 \times 10^{-7}$이 필요한데, 본문은 이 exact value를 제시하지 않는다. Bonferroni "exact $p$"를 제시해야 한다는 요청조차 각주에 포함만 되어 있고 해결되지 않았다. — 치명도 근거: Contribution 3의 "강한 증거" 논조가 "단일 비교 기준 $p < 0.0001$"에만 의존하며, 독자는 본문만 읽으면 Bonferroni 후 생존 여부를 확인할 수 없다.
review/2026-04-17/phase2_redteam_cycle2.md:21:**[Critical] ch1:117 (Figure 1.1 orange box), ch1:153, ch6:27, ch6:132 — 주장: "Pathogen-optimized scoring → 9.36× (H3N2 FUBAR) · Multi-source → 4.012× (H3N2 significance)" (Figure 1.1); "pathogen-optimized scoring achieves up to 9.36× enrichment for H3N2 ($p < 0.0001$)"; "9.36-fold for H3N2 via pathogen-optimized single FUBAR scoring; 3 of 11 pathogens validated" — 공격: Cycle 1에서 지적된 "3 of 11 pathogens"만 평가된 점은 abstract:12, ch4:816, ch6:27에 명시되었지만, 여전히 "pathogen-optimized"라는 단어는 **benchmark에서 사후적(post-hoc)으로 선택된 best scoring**을 의미한다. H3N2의 FUBAR Bayes factor는 Layer A MCC 최적화로 선택되었고, 동일 데이터로 enrichment를 측정한 것은 circular selection이다. ch5:193–196의 "the scoring type identified as optimal by Layer A also achieves the highest vaccine escape enrichment"는 이를 "cross-validation"으로 제시하지만, Layer A와 vaccine escape list는 **동일한 antigenic drift/antibody escape 문헌에서 파생**되므로 독립 validation이 아니다(ch5:195 "Layer A assesses position-level detection accuracy against convergent evolution sites, while vaccine escape enrichment measures the overlap between detected hotspots and experimentally confirmed antibody escape positions" — 두 리스트는 문헌 기반 immune-escape 주석을 공유한다; ch4:747 "88\% immune" for SARS-CoV-2 Layer A 확인). 따라서 "concordance"는 동어반복에 가깝다. — 치명도 근거: Contribution 3의 "독립적 실용 검증" 주장이 성립하지 않으며, 9.36배라는 숫자는 post-hoc selection bias를 포함한 exploratory 결과로 격하되어야 한다.
review/2026-04-17/phase2_redteam_cycle2.md:23:**[Critical] ch4:415 — 주장: "the primary evidence for pathogen-adaptive method selection is not the exact-match rate but the accompanying mean oracle-vs-generalized MCC gap of 0.265 (oracle mean 0.341; generalized mean 0.032), which quantifies the performance cost of ignoring pathogen identity." — 공격: Cycle 1의 "LOPO 0/11 → universal 불가능" 주장을 0.265 MCC gap으로 대체했으나, **0.265 gap의 null distribution이 보고되지 않았다**. 11개 pathogen에서 oracle MCC의 평균은 0.341이고, 각 pathogen에 단일 "average-best" 조합을 적용하면 0.032가 나온다는 수치만 있을 뿐, "무작위 pathogen 할당 하에 기대되는 gap"이 얼마인지 permutation test가 없다. ch3:790 "No family-wise multiple testing correction … was applied to the ANOVA results"로 통계 보정이 생략되었고, ch4:415의 gap 자체도 신뢰구간이나 $p$ 값이 없다. 11개 pathogen으로 11개 oracle을 뽑으면 당연히 oracle > generalized이며, 이것이 "pathogen-adaptive 필요"의 증거가 되려면 최소한 cluster-resampled null distribution 대비 $p$ 값이 필요하다. — 치명도 근거: Contribution 2의 핵심 정량 주장(0.265 MCC gap = 성능 비용)이 통계 유의성 없이 제시된다.
review/2026-04-17/phase2_redteam_cycle2.md:25:**[Critical] abstract:11 / ch4:392 / ch5:284 — 주장: "within-cell residual $\omega^2 \approx 0.39$ remains unmodeled" (abstract:11); "residual variance ($\omega^2_{\text{residual}} \approx 0.39$) represents within-cell variation across the 39 parameter variants within each scoring--family--pathogen combination and measurement noise" (ch4:392); "6-category $\omega^2 = 0.103$ as lower and upper bounds" (ch5:284) — 공격: 잔차 $\omega^2 \approx 0.39 > 0.296$이며, 이는 **모델링되지 않은 분산이 최대 변동원보다 크다**는 사실을 명시한다. 그러나 ch4:390 "largest source of variance, exceeding all main effects and other interactions"와 Abstract "the largest modeled variance component"는 "modeled" 수식어로 얼버무리며, **잔차 $0.39$가 주 효과/상호작용보다 크다는 의미의 "largest single source"로 독자가 오독할 여지**가 남는다. 나아가 ch5:284가 category-level $\omega^2 = 0.103$을 "lower bound"로 제시하며 bracket [0.103, 0.296]을 인정한 것은 정직하지만, Ch6:130 "largest identified modeled variance component"는 modeled의 한계를 소극적으로만 언급하여 cycle 1 수정이 abstract/ch4/ch6 3곳에서 **통일된 강도로 약화되지 않았다**. "within-cell residual $\omega^2 \approx 0.39$ remains unmodeled"만으로는 독자에게 "이게 왜 측정 노이즈로만 해석되는가"가 불명확하다(ch4:392는 "three-way interaction and parameter-variant noise"로 구성된다고 주장하지만, 이 분해 자체가 추정 없이 선언적이다). — 치명도 근거: Contribution 2의 "largest variance source" 서사의 핵심이 "modeled" 한정자 하나에 달려 있으며, 잔차 비율 $0.39/0.85 \approx 46\%$라는 의미를 본문에서 **정량화된 경고로 다루지 않는다**.
review/2026-04-17/phase2_redteam_cycle2.md:29:**[Major] ch1:145, ch6:17 — 주장: "with 9 distinct optimal information types across 11 pathogens and no cross-pathogen generalization (LOPO 0/11)" — 공격: LOPO 0/11을 "no cross-pathogen generalization"으로 번역한 것은 여전히 과대해석이다. ch4:301은 정직하게 "the probability of all 11 being unique by chance is approximately 93\%"를 자인하며 "the more substantive finding is not the uniqueness itself"라고 스스로 약화시켰으나, 그 바로 뒤 ch1:145와 ch6:17의 Contribution 2 소제목은 여전히 LOPO 0/11을 대등한 증거로 병렬 제시한다. 0/11이 chance 93%에서 발생하는 사건이라면 "no cross-pathogen generalization"이라는 절대적 언어는 부적절하며 "limited generalization evidence"가 적절하다. — 치명도 근거: 0/11 수치 자체의 증거가 약하다는 사실을 본문 일부(ch4:301, ch4:415)는 인정하지만, Contribution 2 헤드라인(ch1:145, ch6:17)은 이 약화가 반영되지 않았다.
review/2026-04-17/phase2_redteam_cycle2.md:31:**[Major] ch4:176 — 주장: "Region-level BCa bootstrap CIs~\cite{efron1987better} (1,000 resamplings, $n = 7$ Spike regions; hereafter \emph{region-level BCa CI}) … combination-level BCa CI [0.047, 0.202] … cluster bootstrap CI [0.195, 0.333] for the scoring × pathogen interaction $\omega^2$" — 공격: 세 CI의 명명은 cycle 1에서 지적되어 분리되었으나, **$n = 7$ Spike regions**라는 표본 수가 BCa bootstrap의 적절성을 보장하기에 부족하다는 점은 여전히 논의되지 않는다. Efron(1987)의 BCa는 일반적으로 $n \geq 20$에서 타당하며, $n = 7$에서는 acceleration 파라미터 추정이 불안정하다. [0.323, 0.635]의 폭(0.312)은 ch5:15 "reflect region-dependent recall sensitivity in small samples"로 서술되지만, 이 폭이 BCa의 적합성 자체를 위협한다는 지적은 없다. — 치명도 근거: Stage 1 MutClust-Hybrid 0.778의 통계적 기반이 $n = 7$ region BCa에 의존하며, 이 방법의 robustness 논증이 누락되어 있다.

chapters_en/ch5_adapt.tex:268:\textbf{Contextualizing MCC = 0.083.}
chapters_en/ch5_adapt.tex:269:The modest MCC reflects the inherent difficulty of position-level binary classification under extreme class imbalance (2--5\% positive rate), not a deficiency of the analysis.
chapters_en/ch5_adapt.tex:270:Position-level classification in comparable domains yields similarly low absolute metrics: cancer driver position detection achieves MCC $\approx$ 0.1--0.3~\cite{bailey2018comprehensive}, and transcription factor binding site prediction reports F1 $\approx$ 0.3--0.5~\cite{weirauch2013evaluation}.
chapters_en/ch5_adapt.tex:271:Furthermore, region-overlap analysis (Section~\ref{sec:oracle_mcc_ceiling}) demonstrates that when spatial proximity is considered ($\pm$10 positions), mean oracle MCC increases from 0.289 to 0.712, indicating that detected hotspots are spatially proximate to ground truth even when not exactly overlapping.
chapters_en/ch5_adapt.tex:272:The position-exact MCC thus represents a conservative lower bound; the practical detection accuracy at the region level is substantially higher.
chapters_en/ch5_adapt.tex:281:The oracle ceiling (MCC = 0.160) reveals that even with optimal per-pathogen feature weighting, sequence- and structure-derived features alone cannot fully predict immune escape positions.
chapters_en/ch5_adapt.tex:290:All adaptive strategies performed worse than EqualWeight: kNN-weighted achieved a maximum mean MCC of 0.020, Top-3 AUC 0.049, and Correlation-aware 0.043, compared to EqualWeight's 0.083.
chapters_en/ch5_adapt.tex:295:However, the oracle strategy (mean MCC = 0.160) approximately doubles EqualWeight performance (0.083), confirming that per-pathogen weighting provides genuine improvement when labeled data is available.
chapters_en/ch5_adapt.tex:297:This is a finding about the current state of available data, not a failure of the adaptive concept; the oracle ceiling demonstrates that the potential for adaptive improvement exists and motivates knowledge base expansion as a concrete future direction.
chapters_en/ch5_adapt.tex:306:\item \textbf{Feature heterogeneity}: The most discriminative information type differs across pathogens (5 distinct best features among 12 pathogens), providing a mechanistic explanation for the detection family $\times$ pathogen interaction ($\omega^2 = 0.285$) observed in the ANOVA.
chapters_en/ch5_adapt.tex:307:\item \textbf{Compact core}: A 4-feature core (homoplasy, pLDDT, entropy, frequency) captures 98\% of the full 10-feature ensemble performance under uniform weighting, while features that are noise on average (ESM-2, SASA) are the best discriminators for specific pathogens.
