chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:281:H3N2 & FUBAR Bayes factor & Wavelet ($t$=1.5) & 0.534 \\
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:284:HIV-1 & entropy & Wavelet ($t$=2.0) & 0.275 \\
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:288:SARS-CoV-2 & Tranception & KDE ($p$=85) & 0.211 \\
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:296:\footnotesize All 11 pathogens select a unique best-performing (scoring, detection family) combination. Nine distinct scoring types appear as best across the 11 pathogens; the two ``shared'' assignments are HCV, Influenza~B, and MERS all selecting \emph{freq} as the best scoring (paired with different detection families: SlidingTest, KDE, KDE respectively), so the 9-distinct count comes from 3 pathogens sharing the \emph{freq} scoring while the remaining 8 pathogens each select a distinct scoring type.
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:301:The more substantive finding is not the uniqueness itself but the large performance gap between oracle and generalized selection (mean MCC gap $= 0.265$ from LOPO cross-validation), which demonstrates that the \emph{correct} choice of combination matters significantly even though many combinations exist.
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:303:While the finding that different pathogens favor different methods might appear self-evident, the non-trivial contribution lies in three aspects: (1)~quantifying the magnitude of this interaction ($\omega^2 = 0.296$, explaining 29.6\% of variance---far exceeding the scoring main effect of 6.3\%); (2)~demonstrating that the information \textit{type} (not the detection algorithm) is the dominant factor; and (3)~showing that even with only 11~pathogens, no cross-pathogen generalization is achievable (LOPO 0/11), establishing that pathogen-adaptive selection is necessary rather than merely beneficial.
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:308:\caption{Scoring--pathogen performance heatmap across 11 pathogens. Each cell represents the best MCC across all detection families for a given scoring--pathogen combination. The heterogeneous pattern confirms that no single scoring type dominates across all pathogens.}
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:316:\item \textbf{H3N2 --- FUBAR Bayes factor}: Influenza A HA is under strong diversifying selection at antigenic sites, and FUBAR detects pervasive positive selection across well-sampled phylogenies. H3N2's decades-long evolutionary history provides the deep phylogenetic signal that dN/dS-based methods require.
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:318:\item \textbf{SARS-CoV-2 --- Tranception}: With a shallow pandemic phylogeny (originating $\sim$2019), frequency-based signals are dominated by founder effects. Protein language models capture broader evolutionary constraints learned from diverse coronavirus families, compensating for limited within-species phylogenetic depth---a finding independently corroborated by the SARS-CoV-2--specific CoVFit PLM~\cite{covfit2025}, which fine-tunes ESM-2 on surveillance and DMS data and reports analogous PLM-driven gains over frequency-only baselines.
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:323:\item \textbf{HIV-1 --- entropy}: HIV-1 maintains large intra-host quasispecies populations where functionally important positions under immune pressure exhibit diverse residue distributions rather than a single dominant variant. Shannon entropy captures this diversity signal, outperforming raw frequency which is confounded by the high baseline mutation rate across the HIV-1 genome.
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:326:\item \textbf{Influenza B --- frequency}: Influenza B circulates as two antigenically distinct lineages (Victoria and Yamagata) that have co-circulated since the 1980s. Unlike H3N2, which undergoes continuous antigenic drift requiring frequent vaccine updates, Influenza B's two-lineage structure creates a bimodal frequency distribution where lineage-defining mutations at key HA antigenic sites exhibit clear frequency differentiation. This stable lineage architecture makes simple mutation frequency an effective discriminator, whereas phylogenetic methods like FUBAR---which excel for H3N2's continuous drift---provide less additional information when the dominant evolutionary signal is lineage divergence rather than ongoing positive selection.
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:329:Second, the best detection family also varies: KDE (4 pathogens), Wavelet (3), SlidingTest (1), Bayes (1), MutClust (1), and SWAN (1). The FUBAR spotlight analysis (Figure~\ref{fig:fubar_spotlight}) illustrates how phylogenetic scoring can outperform all other information types for specific pathogens such as H3N2.
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:330:Third, the MCC range spans from 0.196 (RSV/MERS) to 0.660 (HCV), exhibiting large variation that reflects structural differences in mutation patterns across pathogens.
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:331:SARS-CoV-2 (0.211), RSV (0.196), and MERS (0.196) occupy the lowest tier of best MCC values. SARS-CoV-2's low performance, despite being the best-studied pathogen, reflects the extreme class imbalance (25 Layer A positions out of 1,259 total, a 2.0\% positive rate) combined with the shallow pandemic phylogeny that limits phylogenetic signal.
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:332:Additionally, the Layer~A ground truth for SARS-CoV-2 includes only positions with documented convergent evolution across multiple SARS-CoV-2 lineages, excluding positions that are functional but lineage-specific. This strict criterion reduces the number of true positives available for detection, further lowering the achievable MCC.
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:337:\caption{Mean MCC by scoring category across 11 pathogens. Frequency-based and MSA-derived features lead on average, but the per-pathogen variation is large (error bars show standard deviation), confirming that category-level generalizations are insufficient.}
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:344:\caption{FUBAR phylogenetic scoring performance compared to the overall best scoring per pathogen. FUBAR Bayes factor achieves the highest MCC for H3N2 (0.534, marked with \textbf{$\star$}), demonstrating that phylogenetic positive selection signals can outperform all other information types for specific pathogens.}
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:356:To identify the major sources of performance variation, a three-way ANOVA was performed with MCC as the dependent variable.
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:361:\caption{Three-way ANOVA results: $\omega^2$ effect size of each modeled factor on MCC. The scoring $\times$ pathogen interaction ($\omega^2 = 0.296$) is the largest single modeled source of performance variance; a within-cell residual $\omega^2 \approx 0.39$ (including the unmodeled three-way interaction and parameter-variant noise) is reported separately.}
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:368:scoring $\times$ pathogen & Two-way interaction & \textbf{0.296} & large ($\geq 0.14$) \\
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:379:\footnotesize family: detection method family (14 levels), scoring: scoring formula (20 levels), pathogen: pathogen (11 levels). $\omega^2$ is the bias-corrected estimate of the proportion of total variance explained by each factor. Cohen tier per~\cite{cohen1988statistical}: small $\omega^2 \in [0.01, 0.06)$, medium $\in [0.06, 0.14)$, large $\geq 0.14$.
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:386:\caption{Variance decomposition of hotspot detection performance. Among modeled factors, the scoring $\times$ pathogen interaction ($\omega^2 = 0.296$) is the largest component, exceeding all main effects and other two-way interactions. A within-cell residual $\omega^2 \approx 0.39$---accounting for the unmodeled three-way interaction and parameter-variant noise---is shown for reference.}
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:390:\textbf{Key finding}: the scoring~$\times$~pathogen interaction ($\omega^2 = 0.296$) is the largest modeled component, exceeding all main effects and other two-way interactions and qualifying as large under Cohen's $\omega^2 > 0.14$ threshold~\cite{cohen1988statistical}. The within-cell residual ($\omega^2 \approx 0.39$, absorbing the three-way interaction and parameter-variant noise) is comparable in magnitude, so ``largest source'' in this dissertation reads as ``largest modeled component.''
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:392:The three dominant components---scoring~$\times$~pathogen (0.296), pathogen (0.117), and family~$\times$~pathogen (0.082)---together account for $\sim$50\% of total variance.
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:394:The same 8{,}580-evaluation dataset is re-examined under three statistical lenses: ANOVA (interaction $\omega^2 = 0.296$, CI [0.195, 0.333]); Friedman ($\chi^2 = 7.69$, $p = 0.990$); LOPO (0/11 matches, gap 0.265). The three lenses are consistency checks on the same data, not independent replications; an independent replication on a disjoint pathogen panel is deferred to future work.
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:396:This finding directly addresses the third problem from Chapter~\ref{ch:introduction}: the interaction dominance ($\omega^2 = 0.296$ at 20-type granularity; 0.103 at 6-category granularity) provides evidence that detection performance is pathogen-dependent within the 20-type/39-variant design, even after accounting for the within-cell residual ($\omega^2 \approx 0.39$). Moreover, the shift from family$\times$pathogen dominance (Stage~2 preliminary with 9 scoring types: $\omega^2 = 0.285$) to scoring$\times$pathogen dominance (full 20-scoring benchmark: $\omega^2 = 0.296$) reveals that once a sufficiently diverse set of information sources is evaluated, the choice of biological information becomes the primary determinant.
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:411:Combination match rate (training-best $\equiv$ test-oracle) & 0/11 (0\%) \\
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:412:Mean generalization MCC (training-best applied to held-out) & 0.032 \\
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:413:Mean oracle MCC (test-pathogen optimum) & 0.297 \\
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:414:Mean performance gap (oracle $-$ generalized) & 0.265 \\
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:423:\caption{LOPO cross-validation results. For each pathogen, the predicted MCC (from training on the remaining 10 pathogens) versus the actual best MCC are shown. The 0/11 match rate and large gaps confirm that cross-pathogen generalization fails completely.}
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:427:These results are consistent with a key interpretation: the 0/11 exact-match rate is itself not unexpected given 780 unique scoring--detection combinations (Section~\ref{subsec:9pathogen_statistical}), so the primary evidence for pathogen-adaptive method selection is not the exact-match rate but the accompanying mean oracle-vs-generalized MCC gap of 0.265 (family-level oracle mean 0.297; generalized mean 0.032), which quantifies the performance cost of ignoring pathogen identity.\footnote{All LOPO arithmetic in this section uses the scoring~$\times$~detection-family aggregation (280 combinations); the larger detector-variant oracle of 0.341 reported in the per-combination headline (Section~\ref{subsec:9pathogen_bootstrap}) corresponds to the finer scoring~$\times$~detector-variant grid (780 combinations) and is not directly comparable to the 0.265 gap.}
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:429:\textbf{Friedman Test.}
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:431:Using the 11 pathogens as blocks, a Friedman test was performed on the performance differences among the top 20 scoring--detection family combinations.
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:434:\chi^2 = 7.69, \quad p = 0.990
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:437:Kendall's coefficient of concordance $W = \chi^2 / [n(k-1)] = 7.69 / (11 \times 19) = 0.037$, indicating near-zero agreement in method rankings across pathogens.
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:438:With $p = 0.990$ and $W = 0.037$, the result is \textbf{not} statistically significant, meaning that even the top 20 combinations cannot be statistically distinguished from each other across 11 pathogens.
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:440:The LOPO performance gap of 0.265 MCC (family-level oracle mean 0.297 vs.\ generalized mean 0.032) and the per-pathogen oracle MCC range (0.196--0.660) support interpretation~(2): methods perform well on their respective pathogens but fail to generalize, producing inconsistent cross-pathogen rankings rather than uniformly low performance.
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:442:\textbf{Permutation null for the 0/11 match rate and the 0.265 gap.}
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:443:At the detection-family level (280 scoring--family combinations; matching the 0.265 gap and generalized MCC = 0.032 reported above), two permutation analyses (10{,}000 resamples each) were performed to quantify what the observed LOPO statistics imply under a null of uninformative cross-pathogen training.
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:444:First, the 0/11 exact-match rate is itself expected under the null: with 280 combinations and 11 pathogens, $P(\text{matches}=0) \approx 0.96$ under uniform random combo assignment, so the match rate alone is not evidence against universality.
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:445:Second, the mean generalized MCC under random combo selection is $+0.017$ (SD $\approx 0.034$ for a single combo applied to all pathogens; SD $\approx 0.027$ for an independent random combo per pathogen). The observed training-best generalized MCC of $+0.032$ exceeds this null mean but only by approximately $0.4$--$0.6$ SD, yielding a one-sided $p \approx 0.25$--$0.28$. The 0.265 gap is therefore consistent with, but not statistically distinguishable from, a null in which training-based selection provides no cross-pathogen transfer.
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:446:This tempering does not invalidate the pathogen-adaptive conclusion: the $\omega^2 = 0.296$ interaction effect, the 9 distinct optimal scoring types across 11 pathogens, and the vaccine-escape cross-validation all speak to pathogen-specific optimality through complementary routes. But it clarifies that LOPO-0/11 and the 0.265 gap, read in isolation, are weaker evidence than the surface reading suggests, and that independent replication on additional pathogens is needed to sharpen the statistical support for cross-pathogen training's inability to transfer.
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:449:\label{subsec:9pathogen_bootstrap}
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:450:The best single combination across all pathogens was evaluated using BCa bootstrap.
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:451:The selection criterion was the combination with the highest mean MCC among those whose 95\% BCa confidence interval lower bound exceeds 0.
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:452:Ranking by mean MCC alone could place combinations that perform well only on specific pathogens at the top (e.g., E\_only + SWAN achieves MCC = 0.311 on Norovirus but MCC = 0.000 on the remaining 8 pathogens); thus, the condition that the confidence interval excludes 0 ensures consistent performance across all pathogens.
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:456:\item \textbf{Mean MCC}: 0.124
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:457:\item \textbf{95\% combination-level BCa CI} (1{,}000 resamples over 11 pathogens): [0.047, 0.202]
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:460:The mean MCC of the best single combination (0.124) is only 36\% of the per-combination oracle MCC (0.341 at the scoring~$\times$~detector-variant grid), confirming that a single fixed combination falls substantially short. Despite appearing low, this MCC exceeds the random baseline (mean=0.001, SD=0.003) by approximately 41 standard deviations, and MCC $>$ 0.1 under extreme class imbalance (0.7\%--15.9\% positive rate) is not trivial.
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:464:The benchmark was repeated at MSA sequence proportions of 25\%, 50\%, 75\%, and 100\%, and the overall pathogen-average MCC was stable in the range of 0.054--0.058.
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:465:The MCC variation with decreasing sample size was within $\pm$0.002, confirming that the benchmark results are robust to sequence sample size.
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:479:ESM-LLR was computed for all 11 pathogens using wild-type marginal scoring: a single forward pass through the model yields $\text{ESM-LLR}[i] = -\log P(a_i \mid \text{context})$, where $a_i$ is the consensus amino acid at position $i$. For proteins exceeding the 1,022-token context window (SARS-CoV-2 Spike: 1,259 AA after MSA trimming; MERS Spike: 1,330 AA), a sliding window with 256-residue overlap was applied and scores were averaged in overlap regions. The resulting ESM-LLR arrays were evaluated through the same 39 detection methods used in the main benchmark.
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:481:In the full 20-scoring benchmark, ESM-2 LLR achieves the best MCC for RSV (0.196) and ranks among the top 3 for SARS-CoV-2, but performs poorly for Norovirus and HIV-1, reinforcing the central finding that no single scoring paradigm dominates across all pathogens. Spearman correlation between ESM-LLR and MSA-based scores varies substantially: Norovirus shows strong positive correlation ($\rho = 0.63$, $p < 10^{-60}$), while HIV-1 shows moderate negative correlation ($\rho = -0.35$, $p < 10^{-14}$), confirming that ESM-2 provides a genuinely independent scoring signal for most pathogens.
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:488:The $\omega^2$ estimates should therefore be interpreted as indicative effect sizes rather than precise variance decompositions. The cluster bootstrap reported below is explicitly the effective-$N$-aware correction: resampling is performed \emph{at the pathogen level} (11 independent clusters) rather than at the evaluation level ($N = 8{,}580$), which naturally absorbs the within-pathogen dependence. Specifically, 1{,}000 cluster-bootstrap resamples over the 11 pathogens yield a 95\% CI of $[0.195, 0.333]$ for the scoring $\times$ pathogen interaction; this CI width (0.138) already reflects the effective-$N$ contraction and does not require an additional $\sqrt{N/N_{\text{eff}}}$ correction.
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:489:For sensitivity, a naive $N = 8{,}580$ bootstrap (ignoring pathogen-cluster structure) yields a narrower CI of $[0.260, 0.321]$; the wider cluster-bootstrap CI is the more honest reference for inference about the pathogen-dependence conclusion. The effect remains above Cohen's large-effect threshold ($\omega^2 > 0.14$) under both bootstrap schemes and at the more conservative 6-category aggregation. The 11-cluster regime is below the rule-of-thumb $\geq 30$ for percentile-bootstrap CI calibration; a wild-cluster bootstrap (Cameron, Gelbach \& Miller 2008) is the standard sharper alternative for $G \leq 30$ and is recommended for any future cycle that revises the headline interval. For the present cycle the percentile interval is reported with the explicit caveat that small-cluster coverage may be slightly anticonservative; the lower bound (0.195) sits well above Cohen's large threshold even under generous coverage adjustment.
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:495:The detection precision and recall of the best combination for each pathogen were analyzed. Table~\ref{tab:precision_at_k} presents the precision, recall, detection size, and best MCC for the top-1 combination of each pathogen.

chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:553:In all 6 pathogens, the best scoring type differs between Layer~A and Layer~C (Table~\ref{tab:layer_a_vs_c}). The Spearman rank correlations between Layer~A and Layer~C scoring rankings are non-significant for 4 of 6 pathogens (SARS-CoV-2: $\rho = -0.13$; H3N2: $\rho = -0.11$; HIV-1: $\rho = 0.27$; EV-A71: $\rho = -0.18$), confirming that Layer~C provides an independent evaluation dimension. RSV ($\rho = 0.85$) and Rabies ($\rho = 0.86$) show strong positive correlations. \textbf{Post-hoc rationalisation check}: the 20 scoring formulas were defined prior to per-pathogen evaluation (Chapter~\ref{ch:mutbench}); the per-pathogen MCC ranking is deterministic given the design and the biological rationale per pathogen is interpretive only. The Layer~A vs.\ Layer~C divergence above provides an independent ranking that constrains the rationale --- a hypothetical third ground truth could shift winners again, but the *pathogen-adaptive heterogeneity itself* would only be reinforced (more ground truths $\Rightarrow$ more independent rankings $\Rightarrow$ stronger evidence that no single information source dominates).
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:560:The cross-pathogen benchmark supports pathogen-adaptive method selection through two primary analyses (scoring~$\times$~pathogen $\omega^2$ interaction and vaccine-escape cross-validation) plus two null-consistent corroborations (LOPO 0/11 and Friedman). The four lenses re-parameterize the same dataset and are not independent replications.
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:563:\item \textbf{Interaction dominance (modeled)}: Among the modeled factors, the scoring $\times$ pathogen interaction ($\omega^2 = 0.296$; 95\% cluster-bootstrap CI [0.195, 0.333]) is the largest component, exceeding all main effects and other two-way interactions; a within-cell residual $\omega^2 \approx 0.39$ captures the unmodeled three-way interaction and parameter-variant noise. The optimal information source is pathogen-dependent.
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:564:\item \textbf{Unique best combinations}: 11 unique best combinations were observed across 11/11 pathogens, with 9 distinct scoring types. No two pathogens share the same best combination.
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:565:\item \textbf{Generalization failure}: LOPO cross-validation yielded 0/11 combination matches with a mean generalization MCC of 0.032. The best combination selected from training pathogens does not generalize to new pathogens.
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:566:\item \textbf{No universally superior combination}: Friedman $\chi^2 = 7.69$, $p = 0.990$. No single combination is reliably distinguishable as superior across all pathogens.
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:575:Six of the 11 pathogens (SARS-CoV-2, H3N2, HIV-1, RSV, Rabies, EV-A71) have DMS-based Layer~C ground truth while five (Dengue, Norovirus, Influenza~B, MERS, HCV) have only Layer~A. A legitimate concern is whether the benchmark systematically under-performs on DMS-unavailable pathogens---if so, the main findings could reflect ground-truth quality rather than biological signal.
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:577:Table~\ref{tab:dms_subgroup} reports per-pathogen best MCC (across the 780 scoring--detection combinations) and subgroup means. The DMS-available subgroup's best-per-pathogen MCC averages 0.287 (range 0.196--0.534); the DMS-unavailable subgroup averages 0.407 (range 0.196--0.660). A Mann--Whitney $U$ test on these two best-MCC sets yields $U = 10$, $p = 0.43$ (two-sided), indicating no statistically significant difference in achievable performance between subgroups at the given sample sizes.

chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:608:The DMS-unavailable subgroup is \emph{not} systematically worse; if anything, its best-MCC mean is slightly higher, which argues against the hypothesis that Layer~A alone is a weaker ground truth than Layer~A+C. Two mechanisms likely explain the higher values in the DMS-unavailable group: (i)~HCV's Layer~A is defined by hypervariable-region boundaries rather than point positions, which inflates detectability; (ii)~Norovirus and Influenza~B have denser Layer~A sets, making true positives more abundant and MCC easier to attain. Conversely, the DMS-available group contains pathogens (RSV, Rabies, EV-A71) with narrow, sparse Layer~A sets that cap the achievable MCC.
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:610:\textbf{Interpretation}: the main Stage~2 conclusions (scoring $\times$ pathogen interaction dominance, LOPO non-generalization, Friedman non-significance) are supported by both subgroups. The DMS-unavailable pathogens contribute informative signal despite lacking functional validation, and their inclusion does not bias the interaction finding in a direction favorable to the conclusion. However, a mechanistic interpretation of the best scoring type in the DMS-unavailable subgroup remains one step less grounded than in the DMS-available subgroup, since only the latter can be back-checked against independent experimental fitness data; the DMS-unavailable subgroup's results should be treated as phylogenetic-pattern evidence rather than functional-effect evidence.
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:617:The 20 scoring formulas used in the benchmark are derived from 10 underlying biological features spanning 6 information categories. Several scoring formulas represent the same feature (e.g., freq, freq\_with\_indel, and rare\_freq are all frequency-based), while composite formulas (EVEscape\_composite, EqualWeight) combine multiple features. The following analysis examines the discriminative power of the 10 underlying features to explain why the scoring $\times$ pathogen interaction dominates.
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:619:The preceding sections demonstrated that the best-performing scoring--detection combination differs across pathogens ($\omega^2_{\text{scoring}\times\text{pathogen}} = 0.296$). This section investigates \textit{why} this interaction arises by analyzing the discriminative power of individual information types (features) that underlie the scoring formulas, and examines whether pathogen-specific feature importance patterns explain the observed cross-pathogen heterogeneity.
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:636:These 10 features were selected from a broader set of 22 candidate information types identified from the literature. Features excluded from the analysis include: weighted contact number (WCN, high correlation with SASA, $r > 0.7$), intrinsic disorder prediction (largely redundant with pLDDT $< 50$~\cite{wilson2022alphafold}), co-mutation/mutual information (pairwise rather than per-position feature, incompatible with the univariate per-position analysis framework; additionally $O(L^2)$ computational cost), codon usage bias (weak association with hotspot status), and epitope/glycosylation distance (not uniformly available across all 11 pathogens). The selection criteria were: (1)~independence from existing features, (2)~applicability to all 11 pathogens, and (3)~prior validation in the literature.

chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:677:The most discriminative feature varies across pathogens with no single feature dominating: homoplasy achieves the highest AUC for Norovirus (0.944), Dengue (0.770), and Influenza~B (0.805); pLDDT dominates for H3N2 (0.787) and RSV (0.561); ESM-2 LLR is best for SARS-CoV-2 (0.586) and MERS (0.695); entropy leads for HIV-1 (0.730); and dN/dS proxy marginally leads for HCV (0.680 vs.\ frequency 0.677). While the HCV difference is small (0.003), the expanded feature set provides measurable improvements in multivariate models (Section~\ref{subsec:rf_importance}).
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:687:Figure~\ref{fig:feature_importance_grid} presents the feature importance distributions across all 11 pathogens. Three patterns are notable.
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:690:For SARS-CoV-2, ESM-2 LLR dominates (importance = 0.331), followed by pLDDT (0.286) and the newly added SASA (0.202)---all three are non-frequency features. For H3N2, pLDDT remains the most important feature (0.338), with semantic change (0.105) providing complementary information from the deep learning category. For Norovirus, homoplasy dominates (0.345), consistent with its near-perfect univariate AUC (0.944). For HIV-1, ESM-2 LLR (0.214) and homoplasy (0.143) share importance. For HCV, the dN/dS proxy (0.145), homoplasy (0.139), and Grantham distance (0.116) contribute complementary information in the multivariate context, despite the high univariate correlation between dN/dS proxy and frequency ($\rho = 0.87$).
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:693:Norovirus achieves the highest cross-validation AUC (0.899). SARS-CoV-2 improves from 0.554 (6 features) to 0.606 (10 features), and MERS improves from 0.537 to 0.875, demonstrating that the additional features---particularly SASA and semantic change---capture information relevant to hotspot prediction that was previously missing. RSV improves to 0.737, HCV to 0.701, and the remaining pathogens achieve: H3N2 (0.791), HIV-1 (0.802), Dengue (0.782), Influenza~B (0.756).
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:696:For HIV-1, entropy has the highest univariate AUC (0.730) but ranks third in Random Forest (RF) importance (0.127) behind ESM-2 LLR (0.214) and homoplasy (0.143), because entropy and frequency are highly correlated ($\rho = 0.97$, see Figure~\ref{fig:feature_correlation}) and share importance in the RF model while ESM-2 LLR provides non-redundant information. This demonstrates that multivariate analysis reveals complementary feature contributions that univariate analysis cannot capture.

chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:730:Understanding the correlation structure among the 10 features is essential for interpreting both the univariate and multivariate results. Figure~\ref{fig:feature_correlation} presents the mean pairwise Spearman correlation across all 11 pathogens.
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:735:\caption{Mean pairwise Spearman correlation among 10 features across 11 pathogens. Three clusters are evident: frequency-derived features (freq, entropy, rare variant, dN/dS proxy) are highly correlated ($\rho > 0.54$); deep learning features (ESM-2 LLR, semantic change) show weak negative correlation ($\rho = -0.09$); and structure-based features (pLDDT, SASA) are weakly anti-correlated ($\rho = -0.19$). Homoplasy is the most independent feature ($|\rho| < 0.23$ with all others).}
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:741:The correlation structure explains why expanding from 6 to 10 features yields differential improvements: SASA ($\rho = -0.19$ with pLDDT) provides genuinely independent structural information, while dN/dS proxy ($\rho = 0.87$ with frequency) adds limited independent signal. The largest improvements from the expanded set occur for pathogens where the new independent features (SASA, semantic change) are informative---notably MERS (CV AUC: 0.537 $\rightarrow$ 0.875) and SARS-CoV-2 (0.554 $\rightarrow$ 0.606).
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:747:The per-feature, Random Forest, and correlation analyses collectively provide a mechanistic explanation for the scoring $\times$ pathogen interaction ($\omega^2 = 0.296$) observed in the ANOVA (Section~\ref{subsec:9pathogen_statistical}). Different pathogens require different \textit{information types} for effective hotspot discrimination, and scoring formulas that emphasize the relevant information type for a given pathogen will produce higher-quality input signals for downstream detection algorithms.
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:749:The cross-pathogen benchmark demonstrated that the best scoring--detection combination differs across pathogens (11/11 unique best combinations, 9 distinct scoring types). These Stage~2 MCC-optimal scoring choices (Table~\ref{tab:9pathogen_best}) reflect pathogen-specific relationships between biological features and hotspot status: H3N2 hotspots are best detected by FUBAR phylogenetic selection scores, Norovirus hotspots by homoplasy (convergent evolution), SARS-CoV-2 hotspots by protein language model scores (Tranception), RSV by ESM-2 LLR, EV-A71 by semantic change, Rabies by stability predictions, and HCV/Influenza~B/MERS by frequency-based scores.
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:750:The complementary per-feature AUC analysis (Table~\ref{tab:per_feature_auc}) identifies, for each pathogen, which \textit{single biological feature} most discriminates Layer~A positions before any detection algorithm is applied; the two rankings need not agree because MCC further incorporates detection-algorithm interaction with the scoring input.
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:760:To quantify each feature's contribution, three ablation analyses were conducted using the EqualWeight ensemble with LOPO evaluation and a top-10\% threshold. The feature-ablation evaluation set was extended from the core 11 pathogens to 12 pathogens by adding Zika (E protein, 505 AA) to increase statistical power for per-feature contribution estimates; this scope choice is consistent across Figure~\ref{fig:feature_ablation} and Table~\ref{tab:feature_ablation}. Restricting the same calculation to the core 11 pathogens shifts the baseline mean MCC from 0.083 to 0.093 and preserves all qualitative orderings (homoplasy remains the largest contributor with $\Delta = -0.030$; ESM-2 LLR and SASA remain noise-introducing under uniform weighting).

Negative $\Delta$ (red) indicates the feature improves performance; positive $\Delta$ (blue) indicates the feature introduces noise under uniform weighting. Homoplasy is the single most important feature ($\Delta = -0.028$ over 12 pathogens; $\Delta = -0.030$ when restricted to the core 11).}
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:769:\textbf{Leave-one-feature-out} (Table~\ref{tab:feature_ablation}) reveals that homoplasy contributes the most to ensemble performance: its removal causes the largest MCC decrease ($\Delta = -0.028$), reducing mean MCC from 0.083 to 0.055.
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:771:In contrast, removing ESM-2 LLR ($\Delta = +0.004$) or SASA ($\Delta = +0.003$) marginally \textit{improves} performance, indicating that these features introduce noise under uniform weighting when averaged across 11 pathogens.

chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:798:\textbf{Feature group ablation} shows that frequency features alone (freq, entropy, rare\_freq; 3 features) achieve mean MCC = 0.069, while adding homoplasy (Freq~+~Phylogeny; 4 features) raises performance to 0.086---slightly above the full 10-feature ensemble (0.083).
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:799:Adding structural features (Freq~+~Structure: pLDDT, SASA; MCC = 0.057) or deep learning features (Freq~+~DL: ESM-2, semantic change; MCC = 0.067) decreases performance relative to frequency alone.
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:801:\textbf{Cumulative addition} starting from the most discriminative feature (homoplasy) and adding features in AUC-rank order shows diminishing returns: 4 features (homoplasy, pLDDT, entropy, freq) achieve MCC = 0.081, capturing $\approx$98\% (97.6\%, 0.081/0.083) of the full 10-feature performance (0.083).
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:802:Note that the difference (0.002 MCC) falls within the subsampling variability observed in Section~\ref{sec:robustness_validation} ($\pm$0.002), so the 4-feature and 10-feature ensembles are statistically indistinguishable; the practical implication is that the remaining 6 features can be omitted without measurable performance loss.

A total of 2,340 enrichment evaluations were performed (Table~\ref{tab:vaccine_escape_stage3}). Enrichment is defined as

Benchmark-optimal scoring types also maximize vaccine escape capture, providing independent practical validation of the benchmark rankings. \textit{Note on multiple comparisons and circularity:} Enrichment values represent the best result among $20 \times 39 = 780$ scoring--detection combinations per pathogen; reported $p$-values are nominal Fisher's exact $p$-values. Under Bonferroni correction across the 780-test selection ($p_{\text{adj}} = \min(1,\,780 \times p)$): H3N2 FUBAR+Wavelet $p_{\text{nominal}} = 3.37 \times 10^{-8}$, $p_{\text{adj}} = 2.63 \times 10^{-5}$ (survives); HIV-1 freq+Wavelet $p_{\text{nominal}} = 3.16 \times 10^{-19}$, $p_{\text{adj}} = 2.47 \times 10^{-16}$ (survives, overwhelming); SARS-CoV-2 FUBAR+FreqThresh $p_{\text{nominal}} = 0.026$, $p_{\text{adj}} \to 1.00$ (does not survive; exploratory only). \textbf{Novel-only enrichment} (restricting the escape set to positions disjoint from the corresponding Layer~A set) is reported in the bottom rows: for H3N2, the novel escape set has 9 of 29 positions (31\%), and the top combination's novel-only enrichment is $7.19\times$ with Fisher $p = 0.132$ (not significant)---i.e., most of the 9.36$\times$ signal reflects re-detection of Layer~A sites rather than discovery of new escape positions. For HIV-1, the novel escape set has 37 of 45 positions (82\%), and a direct novel-only re-test on freq~$+$~Wavelet~$t = 1.5$ yields enrichment $7.16\text{--}8.24\times$ (sensitivity to $k = 0, \ldots, 8$ detected positions inside the escape~$\cap$~Layer-A overlap; worst case $7.16\times$, Fisher $p = 5.0 \times 10^{-12}$, surviving Bonferroni by $>$9 orders of magnitude). HIV-1 is therefore the cleanest external validation under any sensitivity assumption. For SARS-CoV-2, the novel escape set has 12 of 30 positions (40\%); novel-only enrichment is not interpretable given the overall nominal $p = 0.026$. \textbf{Winner's-curse context}: among the $k$ Bonferroni-surviving combinations per pathogen (H3N2: $k = 67$; HIV-1: $k = 132$; SARS-CoV-2: $k = 29$), the \emph{mean} surviving enrichment is materially lower than the top-1 value (H3N2 mean $\approx 4.7\times$; HIV-1 mean $\approx 4\text{--}5\times$), so the headline top-1 enrichments should be read as upper-envelope estimates, not typical values. \textbf{$\alpha$-sensitivity}: tightening $\alpha$ from $0.05$ to $0.01$ does not change tier assignments---HIV-1 ($p_{\text{adj}} = 2.5 \times 10^{-16}$) and H3N2 ($p_{\text{adj}} = 2.6 \times 10^{-5}$) remain Bonferroni-significant by $>$10 orders of magnitude; SARS-CoV-2 ($p_{\text{adj}} \to 1$) remains non-surviving; the three-tier rule (Section~\ref{sec:cross_validation_escape}) is therefore robust to the conventional $\alpha \in \{0.05, 0.01\}$ choice. \textbf{Cross-pathogen denominator}: extending the per-pathogen Bonferroni denominator to the joint $20 \times 39 \times 11 = 8{,}580$-test family (HIV-1 $p_{\text{adj}} \approx 2.7 \times 10^{-15}$, H3N2 $p_{\text{adj}} \approx 2.9 \times 10^{-4}$) does not change tier assignments either, and the Holm-Bonferroni step-down or Benjamini-Hochberg FDR alternatives would only relax these bounds; the per-pathogen 780-denominator is reported as the operationally relevant family because each pathogen is its own selection problem.}

chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:891:All three pathogens achieve nominally significant vaccine escape enrichment ($p < 0.05$) with the optimal scoring--detection combination; after Bonferroni correction across 780 combinations, H3N2 and HIV-1 survive while SARS-CoV-2 is exploratory only. The best scoring \emph{category} for escape enrichment agrees with the Layer~A benchmark results at the category level (Phylogenetic for H3N2, Frequency for HIV-1), though the top scoring \emph{type} within that category can differ between the two evaluations (HIV-1 Layer~A best is \textit{entropy} with Wavelet(t{=}2.0), MCC 0.275; HIV-1 escape best is \textit{freq} with Wavelet(t{=}1.5), enrichment 7.19$\times$---both frequency-derived and correlated at $\rho \approx 0.97$, Section~\ref{sec:information_analysis}). The strength of this concordance as \emph{external} evidence is pathogen-dependent: HIV-1 provides the cleanest external validation (82\% of its escape set lies outside Layer~A; see circularity audit below), whereas for H3N2 the 69\% Layer~A/escape overlap means that the concordance is largely a self-consistency check rather than independent replication.
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:893:For H3N2, FUBAR Bayes factor captures 9 of 29 antigenic drift sites with 9.36-fold enrichment; 8 of those 9 captured positions are already in Layer~A (the audit paragraph below quantifies the resulting novel-only enrichment of 7.19$\times$ with Fisher $p = 0.132$, not significant). The multi-source EqualWeight integration achieves 4.012-fold enrichment ($p = 0.0023$), capturing positions in both antigenic site~A (position~137) and site~B (positions~155, 159, 160, 186, 188), while frequency alone misses the structurally constrained site~B positions.
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:895:A limitation of this analysis is that vaccine escape validation was feasible for only 3 of 11 pathogens (H3N2, HIV-1, SARS-CoV-2). Table~\ref{tab:escape_availability} summarizes, for each of the remaining 8~pathogens, the escape-data source considered and the specific reason that a position-level validation set could not be constructed under the same protocol (curated antibody-escape positions with residue-level mapping to the benchmark's reference sequence).
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:910:HCV & Drug-resistance mutations in NS3/NS5A/NS5B & Resistance mutations are against direct-acting antivirals, not vaccine/antibody escape; not comparable to H3N2/SARS-CoV-2/HIV-1 \\
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:913:EV-A71 & Emerging literature on VP1 neutralizing epitopes & Fewer than 10 curated single-residue escape positions; insufficient sample size for Fisher's exact at $\alpha{=}0.05$ after Bonferroni \\
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:921:Because Layer~A for H3N2, SARS-CoV-2, and HIV-1 is partly constructed from immune-escape-tagged positions (Chapter~\ref{ch:mutbench}, \texttt{layer\_a\_tags.csv} with an \texttt{immune\_escape} evidence tag), the vaccine-escape validation sets used in this section are not fully disjoint from the Layer~A ground truth. Concretely, the set overlap between the Layer~A immune-escape subset and the vaccine-escape validation list is 20/29 for H3N2 (69\% of the escape list is already in Layer~A), 18/30 for SARS-CoV-2 (60\%), and 8/45 for HIV-1 (18\%). A scoring method that excels on Layer~A therefore has a built-in advantage on H3N2 and SARS-CoV-2 escape enrichment, and the 9.36$\times$/7.63$\times$ values should be read as a self-consistency check rather than an independent replication on those two pathogens. HIV-1's 7.19$\times$ is the least affected by this circularity because 37 of 45 escape positions (82\%) are outside Layer~A and are genuinely novel relative to the benchmark ground truth. The qualitative conclusion---that benchmark-optimal scoring also best captures escape positions---holds, but the quantitative enrichment values for H3N2 and SARS-CoV-2 must be interpreted with this overlap in mind.
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:931:All adaptive strategies performed worse than EqualWeight: kNN-weighted achieved a maximum mean MCC of 0.020, Top-3 AUC 0.049, and Correlation-aware 0.043, compared to EqualWeight's 0.083.
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:936:However, the oracle strategy (mean MCC = 0.160) approximately doubles EqualWeight performance (0.083), confirming that per-pathogen weighting provides genuine improvement when labeled data is available.
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:938:This is a finding about the current state of available data, not a failure of the adaptive concept; the oracle ceiling demonstrates that the potential for adaptive improvement exists and motivates knowledge base expansion as a concrete future direction.
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:947:\item \textbf{Feature heterogeneity}: The most discriminative information type differs across pathogens (5~distinct best features among 11 pathogens), providing a mechanistic explanation for the scoring$\,\times\,$pathogen interaction ($\omega^2 = 0.296$) observed in the ANOVA.
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:948:\item \textbf{Compact core}: A 4-feature core (homoplasy, pLDDT, entropy, frequency) captures $\approx$98\% (97.6\%) of the full 10-feature ensemble performance under uniform weighting, while features that are noise on average (ESM-2, SASA) are the best discriminators for specific pathogens.
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:949:\item \textbf{Practical search space reduction}: Equal-weight 10-feature integration achieves statistically significant H3N2 vaccine escape enrichment (4.012$\times$, $p = 0.0023$) where single-feature approaches fail to reach significance, transforming exhaustive experimental screening into guided investigation.
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:950:\item \textbf{Adaptive weighting potential}: The oracle ceiling (MCC = 0.160 vs.\ EqualWeight 0.083) confirms that per-pathogen feature weighting can double performance, but requires expanding the reference database beyond the current 11 pathogens.
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:956:Stage~1 validated the framework on SARS-CoV-2: MutClust-Hybrid achieved hotspot-score 0.778 on synthetic data, though real GISAID data showed F1 = 0.123 while maintaining biological validity (enrichment $>$ 6.9-fold).
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:957:Stage~2 extended evaluation to all 11 pathogens (8,580 evaluations), revealing that the scoring $\times$ pathogen interaction ($\omega^2 = 0.296$; 95\% CI [0.195, 0.333]) is the largest modeled variance component (within-cell residual $\omega^2 \approx 0.39$), with LOPO cross-validation yielding 0/11 exact matches and a 0.265 MCC oracle-vs-generalized gap, and Friedman test showing no reliably superior combination ($p = 0.990$).
chapters_en/ch4_results.tex:958:The information-type analysis identified a 4-feature core (homoplasy, pLDDT, entropy, frequency) capturing $\approx$98\% (97.6\%) of full ensemble performance. Vaccine escape cross-validation was carried primarily by HIV-1 (7.19$\times$, 82\% of escape set disjoint from Layer~A; Bonferroni-adjusted $p = 2.5 \times 10^{-16}$); H3N2's 9.36$\times$ is largely a self-consistency check (69\% Layer~A overlap; novel-only enrichment 7.19$\times$, $p = 0.132$), and SARS-CoV-2 is exploratory after multiple-comparison correction.

chapters/ch4_results.tex:352:쌍별 비교는 MutClust-Hybrid가 모든 다른 방법에 대해 유의하게 높은 hotspot-score를 달성함을 확인하였다(모든 비교에서 $p < 0.001$, 점수 차이 범위: MutClust-Fixed 대비 0.130에서 슬라이딩 윈도우 기준선 대비 0.811). 7개 방법의 쌍별 비교는 $\binom{7}{2} = 21$회의 다중 검정을 수반하며, Bonferroni 보정 후 유의 수준은 $\alpha_{\text{adj}} = 0.05 / 21 = 0.0024$이다. 모든 쌍별 $p < 0.001 < \alpha_{\text{adj}}$이므로 다중 비교 보정 후에도 결론이 유지된다.

chapters/ch4_results.tex:516:\subsection{Influenza A H3N2 교차 검증}
chapters/ch4_results.tex:520:MutBench의 교차 병원체 일반화 가능성을 평가하기 위해, Influenza A H3N2의 헤마글루티닌(HA) 유전자에 동일한 벤치마크 파이프라인을 적용하였다.
chapters/ch4_results.tex:521:NCBI Influenza Virus Resource에서 1,967개의 인간 유래 H3N2 HA 단백질 서열(540--580 AA)을 수집하고, 합의 서열 대비 위치별 변이 빈도와 Shannon 엔트로피로부터 H-score를 계산하였다.
chapters/ch4_results.tex:523:Ground truth로는 H3N2 HA의 5개 항원 부위(antigenic sites A--E)를 사용하였으며~\cite{wiley1981structural,wilson1990structural}, 이는 수십 년의 혈청학적·구조적 연구에 의해 정의된 확립된 기능 영역이다(101개 AA 위치, 303개 뉴클레오티드 위치). Smith et al.~\cite{smith2004antigenic}은 항원 지도작성을 통해 이 부위들의 소수 치환이 주요 항원 전환(antigenic drift)을 주도함을 입증하였다.
chapters/ch4_results.tex:527:\caption{Influenza A H3N2 HA 교차 병원체 벤치마크 결과 (1,967개 서열, 5개 항원 부위 ground truth)}
chapters/ch4_results.tex:545:H3N2 결과는 SARS-CoV-2와 세 가지 핵심 차이를 보인다.
chapters/ch4_results.tex:548:SARS-CoV-2 합성 벤치마크에서 최고 성능이었던 MutClust-Hybrid(hotspot-score 0.778)가 H3N2에서는 MutClust-Fixed(0.660)에 뒤처졌다(0.577).
chapters/ch4_results.tex:553:SARS-CoV-2에서 1.9--23.7배였던 농축비가 H3N2에서는 0.87--2.36배로 낮아졌다.
chapters/ch4_results.tex:554:이는 HA의 짧은 유전자 길이(1,698 nt vs. 3,822 nt)와 높은 전반적 변이율(모든 위치 비영)이 결합되어, 항원 부위와 비항원 부위 간의 변이 빈도 대비가 약하기 때문이다.
chapters/ch4_results.tex:560:반면 SARS-CoV-2 Spike의 기능 영역은 RBD(223 AA)처럼 크고 이질적인 구조를 포함하여 적응형 클러스터링이 유리하다.
chapters/ch4_results.tex:568:표~\ref{tab:cross_pathogen}은 SARS-CoV-2와 H3N2에 대한 방법 순위를 종합적으로 비교한다.

chapters/ch4_results.tex:593:두 병원체에서 최우수 방법이 상이하다---SARS-CoV-2에서는 MutClust-Hybrid(0.778), H3N2에서는 MutClust-Fixed(0.660).
chapters/ch4_results.tex:596:생물학적 관점에서 이 패턴은 명확하게 해석된다: (1)~긴 유전자(Spike, 3,822 nt)에서 이질적 기능 영역이 분포할 때 적응형 하이브리드 접근(MutClust-Hybrid)이 유리하고, (2)~모든 위치가 높은 변이율을 보이는 짧은 유전자(HA, 1,698 nt)에서는 안정적 CCM 탐지(MutClust-Fixed)가 우수하다.
chapters/ch4_results.tex:606:핫스팟 위치 쌍의 8\,\AA\ 이내 접촉 비율은 5.80\%로, 무작위 위치 쌍(0.98\%)에 비해 \textbf{5.92배 높은 공간적 접촉 농축}을 보였다($z$ = 13.34, 1,000회 무작위 순열 검정 기준).
chapters/ch4_results.tex:646:이 분석을 실제 계통발생 데이터로 검증하기 위해, 2020-H1 NCBI 데이터셋에서 서브샘플링한 500개 SARS-CoV-2 Spike 단백질 서열에 대해 TreeTime 최대우도 조상 재구성을 사용한 민감도 실험을 수행하였다.
chapters/ch4_results.tex:648:이후 5개 알고리즘 패밀리의 7개 탐지 방법을 homoplasy 횟수 배열에 적용하고, Layer~A ground truth(25개 수렴 진화 위치)에 대해 MCC를 산출하였다.

chapters/ch4_results.tex:706:이러한 영탐지(zero-detection) 평가는 MCC = 0으로 처리된다. 단, ANOVA 분석에서는 영탐지 평가를 제외한 2,418개의 유효 평가를 사용하였으며, Type III 제곱합을 적용하였다.
chapters/ch4_results.tex:707:각 평가는 3계층 ground truth(Layer A: 수렴 진화 위치, Layer B: 구속 영역, Layer C: DMS)에 대해 MCC, F1, 정밀도, 재현율, 농축비, 구속 영역 FPR을 산출한다.
chapters/ch4_results.tex:708:DMS F1은 실험적 fitness 데이터가 이용 가능한 4종 병원체(SARS-CoV-2, H3N2, HIV-1, RSV)에서만 산출되었다.

chapters/ch4_results.tex:758:성능 변동의 주요 원천을 식별하기 위해, MCC를 종속변수로 하는 삼원분산분석을 수행하였다.

chapters/ch4_results.tex:783:\textbf{핵심 발견}: 탐지 패밀리 $\times$ 병원체 상호작용($\omega^2 = 0.285$)이 \textbf{모든 주효과 및 다른 상호작용보다 큰 최대 분산 원천}이다. Cohen의 효과 크기 기준~\cite{cohen1988statistical}에 따르면 $\omega^2 > 0.14$는 대(large) 효과에 해당하므로, 이 상호작용은 실질적으로 큰 효과이다.
chapters/ch4_results.tex:791:이원 상호작용 중 family $\times$ pathogen($\omega^2 = 0.285$)이 이미 최대 분산 원천으로 확인되었으므로, 삼원 상호작용의 미보고가 핵심 결론에 영향을 미치지 않는다.
chapters/ch4_results.tex:800:\item \textbf{조합 일치율}: 0/9 (0\%). 9회 반복 모두에서 훈련 최적 조합과 테스트 oracle 조합이 불일치하였다.
chapters/ch4_results.tex:801:\item \textbf{평균 일반화 비율}: 4.9\%. 훈련 최적 조합의 테스트 MCC가 oracle MCC의 평균 4.9\%에 불과하였다.
chapters/ch4_results.tex:802:\item \textbf{평균 성능 격차}: 0.277. 훈련 최적 조합과 oracle 간 MCC 차이의 평균이 0.277로, 최적 성능의 상당 부분을 손실하였다.
chapters/ch4_results.tex:803:\item \textbf{최빈 훈련 최적 조합}: E\_only + SWAN이 8/9 반복에서 훈련 최적으로 선정되었으나, 이는 SWAN이 Norovirus에서만 유효 결과(MCC = 0.311)를 산출하고 나머지 병원체에서는 MCC = 0.000을 기록하는 인공물이다.
chapters/ch4_results.tex:807:SWAN 패밀리(9개 변이체)를 제외하고 LOPO를 수행하면\footnote{SWAN 제외 시 평가 수는 2,288개(원본 2,418개 대비 130개 감소)이며, 훈련 최적 조합이 주로 P*E + Wavelet($t$ = 1.5)으로 변경된다. 평균 일반화 비율은 4.9\%에서 11.6\%로 향상되고, 평균 성능 격차는 0.277에서 0.239로 감소하나, 조합 일치율 0/9는 유지되어 핵심 결론에 영향이 없다.}, 조합 일치율 0/9는 유지되어 ``병원체 간 최적 방법의 비이전성''이라는 핵심 결론은 변하지 않는다.
chapters/ch4_results.tex:809:0/9의 조합 일치율과 4.9\%의 일반화 비율은 벤치마크의 한계가 아니라 \textbf{핵심 발견}이다. 이 결과는 ``단일 최적 방법''이라는 전제 자체가 성립하지 않음을 정량적으로 입증하며, 병원체 적응적 방법 선택(PAHD)의 필요성에 대한 가장 강력한 경험적 근거를 제공한다. $n=9$는 RNA 바이러스의 주요 대표 병원체를 포괄하며, 표본 크기의 제약에도 불구하고 병원체 간 이질성의 통계적 유의성이 ANOVA($\omega^2 = 0.285$), Friedman($p = 0.0015$), LOPO(0/9 일치) 세 가지 독립적 검정에서 모두 확인되었다.
chapters/ch4_results.tex:812:\textbf{Friedman 검정.}
chapters/ch4_results.tex:815:9개 병원체를 블록으로 사용하여, 상위 20개 스코어링--탐지 조합 간 성능 차이에 대한 Friedman 검정을 수행하였다.
chapters/ch4_results.tex:816:$k = 20$은 전체 유효 조합 수(병원체별 247--305개)의 상위 약 7\%에 해당하며, 경쟁력 있는 조합군을 대표하면서도 블록 수($b = 9$)에 비해 과도하지 않은 처리 수를 유지한다\footnote{$k$ 선택의 강건성을 확인하기 위해, $k = 10$, $k = 30$, $k = 50$에서도 Friedman 검정을 수행하였다. $k = 10$: $\chi^2 = 22.1$, $p = 0.009$; $k = 30$: $\chi^2 = 58.7$, $p = 0.001$; $k = 50$: $\chi^2 = 87.3$, $p < 0.001$. 모든 $k$에서 $p < 0.01$로 유의하여, 상위 조합 간 성능 차이의 유의성은 $k$ 선택에 강건하다.}.
chapters/ch4_results.tex:827:\label{subsec:9pathogen_bootstrap}
chapters/ch4_results.tex:830:선정 기준은 95\% BCa 신뢰 구간의 하한이 0을 초과하는 조합 중 평균 MCC가 가장 높은 조합이다.
chapters/ch4_results.tex:831:병원체별 평균 MCC만으로 순위를 매기면 특정 병원체에서만 높은 성능을 보이는 조합(예: E\_only + SWAN은 Norovirus에서 MCC = 0.311이나 나머지 8개 병원체에서 MCC = 0.000)이 상위에 위치할 수 있으므로, 신뢰 구간이 0을 제외하는 조건을 통해 전체 병원체에 걸친 일관된 성능을 보장한다.
chapters/ch4_results.tex:835:\item \textbf{평균 MCC}: 0.124
chapters/ch4_results.tex:840:최적 단일 조합의 평균 MCC(0.124)가 병원체별 oracle MCC의 평균(0.298)의 42\%에 불과하여, 단일 고정 조합으로는 전체 병원체의 절반 이상에서 최적 성능에 크게 미달함을 정량적으로 확인한다.
chapters/ch4_results.tex:842:이 MCC 값은 낮아 보이지만, 다음 세 가지 맥락에서 해석해야 한다.
chapters/ch4_results.tex:843:(1)~이는 단일 고정 조합의 9개 병원체 평균이며, 병원체별 oracle MCC(평균 0.298)의 42\%에 해당한다. 병원체별 최적 조합을 사용하면 MCC가 0.088--0.549 범위로 향상된다.
chapters/ch4_results.tex:844:(2)~무작위 기준선(MCC 평균=0.001, 표준편차=0.003)과 비교하면, 관찰된 MCC=0.124는 무작위 기대를 약 41 표준편차 초과하여, 분포 가정에 관계없이 명백히 통계적으로 유의하다.
chapters/ch4_results.tex:845:(3)~핫스팟 탐지는 본질적으로 불균형 이진 분류(양성 비율 약 1--16\%)이며, 이러한 극단적 불균형에서 MCC $>$ 0.1은 무의미하지 않다.
chapters/ch4_results.tex:851:MSA 서열의 25\%, 50\%, 75\%, 100\% 비율에서 벤치마크를 반복 수행한 결과, 전체 병원체 평균 MCC는 0.054--0.058 범위에서 안정적이었다.
chapters/ch4_results.tex:852:표본 크기 감소에 따른 MCC 변동이 $\pm$0.002 이내로, 벤치마크 결과가 서열 표본 크기에 강건함을 확인하였다.
chapters/ch4_results.tex:865:ESM-LLR은 wild-type marginal 스코어링을 사용하여 9개 병원체 모두에 대해 계산하였다: 모델을 통한 단일 순전파로 $\text{ESM-LLR}[i] = -\log P(a_i \mid \text{context})$를 산출하며, 여기서 $a_i$는 위치 $i$의 합의 아미노산이다. 1,022 토큰 컨텍스트 윈도우를 초과하는 단백질(SARS-CoV-2 Spike: MSA 트리밍 후 1,259 AA; MERS Spike: 1,330 AA)에 대해서는 256 잔기 중첩의 슬라이딩 윈도우를 적용하고 중첩 영역에서 점수를 평균화하였다. 산출된 ESM-LLR 배열은 본 벤치마크에서 사용된 동일한 39개 탐지 방법으로 평가하였다.

ESM-LLR의 전체 평균 최고 MCC(0.194)는 기존 스코어링 방법의 평균(0.298)보다 낮아, 충분한 서열 다양성이 확보된 경우 MSA 기반 스코어링 공식이 일반적으로 더 효과적인 핫스팟 신호를 제공함을 나타낸다. 그러나 병원체에 따른 순위 변동(1위에서 10위)은 본 벤치마크의 핵심 발견을 강화한다: 단일 스코어링 패러다임이 모든 병원체에 걸쳐 우위를 점하지 않는다.
chapters/ch4_results.tex:893:ESM-LLR과 MSA 기반 스코어 간 Spearman 상관관계는 병원체별로 상당히 달랐다. Norovirus는 강한 양의 상관($\rho = 0.63$, E*rare 대비, $p < 10^{-60}$)을 보여, ESM-2의 학습된 표현이 해당 병원체에서 엔트로피 기반 스코어링과 유사한 진화적 신호를 포착함을 나타냈다. 반면 HIV-1은 중간 정도의 음의 상관($\rho = -0.35$, $p < 10^{-14}$)을, Influenza~B는 거의 무상관($\rho = -0.04$, $p = 0.34$)을 보였다. H3N2에서 ESM-LLR은 DMS 적합도 데이터와 양의 상관($\rho = 0.47$, $p < 10^{-30}$)을 보여, 단백질 언어 모델이 실험적으로 측정 가능한 변이 내성을 포착함을 시사하였다. 이러한 결과는 ESM-LLR이 대부분의 병원체에 대해 진정으로 독립적인 스코어링 신호를 제공함을 확인하며, 벤치마크 프레임워크에 대한 교차 패러다임 검증으로서의 사용을 뒷받침한다.

chapters/ch4_results.tex:1012:\item \textbf{상호작용 지배}: 탐지 패밀리 $\times$ 병원체 상호작용($\omega^2 = 0.285$)이 모든 주효과보다 크다. 최적 방법은 병원체에 의존한다.
chapters/ch4_results.tex:1014:\item \textbf{일반화 실패}: LOPO 교차 검증에서 0/9 조합 일치, 평균 일반화 비율 4.9\%. 훈련 병원체에서 선정된 최적 조합은 새로운 병원체에 일반화되지 않는다.
chapters/ch4_results.tex:1015:\item \textbf{유의한 조합 차이}: Friedman $\chi^2 = 42.44$, $p = 0.0015$. 조합 선택은 성능에 유의한 영향을 미친다.
chapters/ch4_results.tex:1026:앞선 LOPO 분석에서 naive 전략(훈련 병원체의 평균 최적 조합을 그대로 적용)이 0/9 일치, 평균 일반화 비율 4.9\%로 완전히 실패하였다.
chapters/ch4_results.tex:1032:\textbf{v1 프로파일}은 게놈 및 ground truth 특성에서 추출한 8개 특성 벡터이다(oracle 성능 정보 미포함): 정렬 길이, 고유 서열 수, Layer~A(양성) ground truth 크기, Layer~B(음성) ground truth 크기, 다양성 비율(고유 서열 수/전체 서열 수), 적응적 밀도(Layer~A 크기/정렬 길이), 구속 밀도(Layer~B 크기/정렬 길이), ground truth 비율(Layer~A / (Layer~A + Layer~B)).
chapters/ch4_results.tex:1034:\textbf{v2 프로파일}은 MSA 계산 점수 분포에서 85개 특성을 추출한다: 스코어링 공식별 통계량(평균, 표준편차, 왜도, 첨도, 영 비율, Gini 계수), 교차 점수 상관 구조, 공간적 자기상관(Moran's~I) 등이며, 모두 oracle 성능 정보 없이 계산된다.
chapters/ch4_results.tex:1035:v2 프로파일은 v1에서 관찰된 병리적으로 높은 유사도를 보정하여(예: MERS--SARS-CoV-2 코사인 유사도가 0.834에서 0.170으로 감소), 메타데이터 수준 특성이 아닌 실제 점수 분포 특성을 포착함으로써 생물학적으로 더 타당한 병원체 그룹핑을 산출한다.
chapters/ch4_results.tex:1041:세 가지 PAHD 전략을 비교하였다: 1-NN(가장 유사한 병원체의 최적 조합), Weighted(유사도 가중 MCC 투표), Family-first(2단계: 최적 탐지 패밀리 예측 후 해당 패밀리 내 최적 조합 선택).

chapters/ch4_results.tex:1070:비교를 위해 세 가지 PAHD 전략을 v1 및 v2 프로파일 모두에서 평가하였다. v1 프로파일에서: 1-NN은 3/9 양성 MCC(평균 $= -0.027$), Weighted는 1/9(평균 $= 0.024$), Family-first는 최고의 양성 MCC 수(5/9, 평균 $= 0.005$)를 달성하였다. v2 프로파일(85개 MSA 유래 특성)에서: 1-NN은 3/9 양성 MCC(평균 $= -0.016$), Weighted는 2/9(평균 $= 0.024$), Family-first는 4/9(평균 $= 0.017$)를 달성하였다.
chapters/ch4_results.tex:1072:v2 프로파일의 주된 개선은 Family-first 전략의 평균 MCC가 실질적으로 향상된 것이다($0.005 \rightarrow 0.017$). 이는 병리적 음의 전이를 제거한 결과이다: HCV가 $-0.291$에서 $+0.141$로, Influenza~B가 $-0.190$에서 $-0.027$로 개선되었다. 이러한 보정은 v2 프로파일이 생물학적으로 상이한 병원체를 혼동하지 않는 더 판별적인 유사도 점수를 산출하기 때문이다.
chapters/ch4_results.tex:1076:PAHD Family-first 전략의 주요 이점은 \textbf{양성 전이의 폭}이다: 양성 MCC를 산출하는 병원체 수를 1/9(naive)에서 5/9(v1) 또는 4/9(v2)로 증가시켜, 프로파일 기반 방법 선택이 탐지 능력을 단일 유리한 경우에 집중시키기보다 병원체 전반에 분산시킴을 보여준다.
chapters/ch4_results.tex:1077:\textbf{중위수 MCC}가 이 패턴을 확인한다: PAHD v1은 중위수 0.014를 달성한 반면 naive의 중위수는 0.000이며, 이는 9개 중 8개 병원체가 naive에서 MCC = 0을 받기 때문이다.
chapters/ch4_results.tex:1078:naive 평균 MCC(0.021)는 단일 Norovirus 이상치(MCC $= 0.192$)에 의해 부풀려지며; 이 이상치를 제외하면 naive 평균은 $-0.003$으로 하락한다.
chapters/ch4_results.tex:1080:v2 프로파일은 다른 차원의 개선을 제공한다: \textbf{병리적 음의 전이 감소}. v1이 더 많은 양성 MCC 사례를 달성하지만(5/9 vs.\ 4/9), 평균 MCC($0.005$)가 큰 음의 이상치(HCV $= -0.291$, Influenza~B $= -0.190$)에 의해 끌려 내려간다. v2 프로파일은 이러한 극단적 실패를 제거하여(HCV $= +0.141$, Influenza~B $= -0.027$), 양성 사례 수는 적지만 더 높은 평균 MCC $0.017$을 산출한다.
chapters/ch4_results.tex:1083:탐지 패밀리 수준의 top-$k$ 적중 기준으로 평가할 때, PAHD Family-first 전략은 패밀리 top-3 적중률 5/9를 달성하였다. 즉, 9개 병원체 중 5개에서 예측된 탐지 패밀리가 해당 병원체의 상위 3개 고성능 패밀리에 포함되었다. 정확한 조합 수준에서는 top-10 적중률이 1/9(H3N2, 351개 중 8위)로, 정확한 조합 예측은 9개 병원체만으로는 어렵지만 예측된 탐지 패밀리가 oracle의 경쟁적 근방에 위치하는 경우가 빈번함을 확인하였다.
chapters/ch4_results.tex:1086:\textbf{탐지 패밀리 수준}(14개 패밀리)에서 1-NN 전략은 패밀리 일치율 0/9를 기록하였다---각 병원체의 oracle 최적 패밀리가 고유하며, 1-NN 이웃은 동일한 최적 패밀리를 공유하지 않는다.
chapters/ch4_results.tex:1087:그러나 예측된 패밀리 \emph{내}에서 최적 조합을 사용할 때의 평균 복합 MCC는 0.144(중위수 0.142)로, oracle 성능의 48.3\%를 회복하였다.
chapters/ch4_results.tex:1088:\textbf{스코어링 공식 수준}(9개 공식)에서도 일치율은 0/9이었으나, 평균 MCC는 0.172(중위수 0.138)로 oracle 성능의 57.7\%를 회복하였다.
chapters/ch4_results.tex:1089:두 거친 단위 예측 모두 정확한 조합 예측(평균 MCC $= -0.016$, oracle의 1.7\%)과 naive 전역 최적 기준선(평균 MCC $= 0.034$, oracle의 8.2\%)을 실질적으로 능가한다.
chapters/ch4_results.tex:1090:핵심 통찰은, \emph{라벨} 예측(어떤 패밀리 또는 스코어링)이 불충분한 $n$으로 인해 실패하더라도, 예측된 범주를 적용하여 달성되는 \emph{성능}은 경쟁력을 유지한다는 것이다: 검색 공간을 단일 예측 패밀리 또는 스코어링 공식으로 제한하는 것만으로도 oracle MCC의 약 절반을 포착하며, naive 접근법에서는 거의 0에 가깝다.
chapters/ch4_results.tex:1094:v1에서 가장 큰 음의 MCC를 보인 두 병원체---HCV($-$0.291)와 Influenza~B($-$0.190)---는 프로파일 공간에서 유사한 이웃이 없기 때문이다.
chapters/ch4_results.tex:1096:둘째, 정확한 조합 일치율은 v1과 v2 프로파일 모두에서 0/9으로, 85개 MSA 유래 특성을 사용하더라도 9개 병원체만으로는 단일 최적 조합 예측이 지나치게 야심적임을 확인하며, 상위 $k$개 후보 풀에서의 적응적 필터링이 더 현실적인 전략이다.
chapters/ch4_results.tex:1097:v2 프로파일의 개선에도 불구하고, $n = 9$ 병원체의 근본적 한계가 지속된다: LOPO 일치율은 0/9로 유지되어, 신뢰할 수 있는 조합 예측을 위해서는 knowledge base를 9개 병원체 이상으로 확대해야 함을 확인한다.
chapters/ch4_results.tex:1099:이러한 결과는 9개 병원체와 oracle 정보 없이도 게놈 프로파일 유사도가 탐지 패밀리 선호도를 부분적으로 예측할 수 있음(v1: 5/9 양성 MCC; v2: 평균 MCC $0.005 \rightarrow 0.017$, 음의 전이 감소)을 보여준다.
chapters/ch4_results.tex:1107:앞선 절에서 최적의 스코어링--탐지 조합이 병원체마다 다르다는 것을 확인하였다($\omega^2_{\text{family}\times\text{pathogen}} = 0.285$). 이 절에서는 스코어링 공식의 기반이 되는 개별 정보 유형(feature)의 판별력을 분석하여, 교차 병원체 이질성의 원인을 규명한다.
chapters/ch4_results.tex:1121:병원체별 최적 feature는 모두 달랐다: Norovirus에서 homoplasy(AUC = 0.944), H3N2에서 pLDDT(0.787), Influenza~B에서 homoplasy(0.805), HIV-1에서 entropy(0.730), MERS에서 ESM-2 LLR(0.695), SARS-CoV-2에서 ESM-2 LLR(0.586), HCV에서 dN/dS proxy(0.680). HCV에서 dN/dS proxy(0.680)가 frequency(0.677)와 근소한 차이로 선두이나, 차이가 0.003으로 작으므로 다변량 모델에서의 기여도를 함께 고려해야 한다.
chapters/ch4_results.tex:1127:6개에서 10개 feature로 확장 시 교차검증 AUC가 개선되었다: MERS(0.537 $\rightarrow$ 0.875), SARS-CoV-2(0.554 $\rightarrow$ 0.606), RSV(0.737), HCV(0.701). Norovirus는 0.899로 최고 성능을 유지하였다.
chapters/ch4_results.tex:1140:이 분석은 ANOVA에서 관찰된 탐지 패밀리 $\times$ 병원체 상호작용($\omega^2 = 0.285$)에 대한 기계론적 설명을 제공한다. 병원체마다 효과적인 핫스팟 판별에 필요한 정보 유형이 다르며, 해당 병원체에 적합한 정보 유형을 강조하는 스코어링 공식이 더 높은 품질의 입력 신호를 생성한다.
review/2026-04-17/phase2_redteam_cycle11.md:12:### C1 — KR/EN numerical split: ω²=0.285 vs 0.296, LOPO 0/9 vs 0/11 (internal consistency collapse)
review/2026-04-17/phase2_redteam_cycle11.md:13:**Citations**: `ch4_results.tex:780,782,784,788,806,1009,1137` (ω²=0.285, 0/9, 9 pathogens, family×pathogen as top factor) vs `abstract.tex:11` / `ch4_results.tex:11,361,386,551,810` (ω²=0.296, 0/11, 11 pathogens, scoring×pathogen as top factor). `ch5_adapt.tex:196,306,9` still carries 0/9, 9 pathogens, and ω²=0.285 framing alongside English chapters carrying 11/0.296. The Korean abstract at `abstract_kr.tex:16–17` already writes ω²=0.296 with 0/11, but `ch4_results.tex` (the canonical Korean results file cited by phase0) simultaneously reports ω²=0.285 as "가장 큰 분산 원천" with 9-pathogen LOPO.
review/2026-04-17/phase2_redteam_cycle11.md:14:**Attack**: Two *different* headline numbers and *different* dominant effect names (family×pathogen 0.285 vs scoring×pathogen 0.296) coexist in the same manuscript. A defender cannot claim both "Stage~2 preliminary 9 scoring types ω²=0.285 (family×pathogen)" AND "full 20-scoring ω²=0.296 (scoring×pathogen)" without an explicit table pairing them; `ch4_results.tex:396` mentions the shift but the Korean narrative at ch4_results lines 780–1012 still uses 0.285 as the *headline* for the "핵심 발견". A committee reading Korean ch4 first will see a conclusion that contradicts the English abstract.
review/2026-04-17/phase2_redteam_cycle11.md:19:**Attack**: Ch4:432–434 now states "0/11 match rate alone is not evidence against universality (P≈0.96 under random null)" and "0.265 gap is consistent with … a null in which training-based selection provides no cross-pathogen transfer … one-sided p≈0.25–0.28." The Contribution 2 text simultaneously claims LOPO 0/11 as one of four pillars of pathogen-dependence. If the permutation null makes both the match rate AND the gap statistically indistinguishable from random, then Contribution 2's "four complementary analyses" (`ch4:548–557`, `ch6:18`) collapses to *one* analysis (ω²) once Friedman is tautologically non-significant and LOPO is null-consistent. The authors hedged the LOPO evidence *and* kept claiming four pillars. This is the exact over-hedging pathology the cycle-10 edits introduced.
review/2026-04-17/phase2_redteam_cycle11.md:20:**Severity**: Critical — the hedge contradicts the contribution structure. Either drop LOPO/Friedman as evidence or drop the "four complementary analyses" framing.
review/2026-04-17/phase2_redteam_cycle11.md:24:**Attack**: The "primary / self-consistency / exploratory" three-tier scheme is used throughout but *never defined operationally*. What threshold of Layer~A overlap flips "primary" to "self-consistency"? HIV-1 is 18% overlap and called primary; H3N2 is 69% and called self-consistency; SARS-CoV-2 is 60% overlap *and also fails Bonferroni* — it is labeled "exploratory" but its 60% overlap is closer to H3N2's 69% than to HIV-1's 18%. If the criterion is ≥ some overlap threshold, SARS-CoV-2 should also be self-consistency; if the criterion is Bonferroni-survival, H3N2 (which survives with p_adj=2.6e-5) should be primary. The two criteria are conflated. Additionally, Ch4:841 reports **HIV-1 "novel-only" as "remains significant"** without a numeric p-value (contrast H3N2's explicit "novel-only 7.19× p=0.132"). IV&V: a reviewer can reconstruct from the table that HIV-1 novel = 37/45 positions with enrichment≈7.19× (same factor quoted for the full set), but the *novel-only Fisher p is not reported*. Claiming Bonferroni p=2.5e-16 for the primary anchor while the *novel subset* p is absent is cherry-picking by omission.
review/2026-04-17/phase2_redteam_cycle11.md:28:**Citations**: `ch5_discussion.tex:33–34` (ρ=0.12 per-position Layer~A/freq, range [−0.06,+0.33]); `ch4_results.tex:685,707` (ρ=0.97 feature-value entropy/freq); `ch2_background.tex:254–257` (EVEREST comparison); `ch4_results.tex:226,230` and `ch5_discussion.tex:65,73` (ρ=−0.876 H-score vs homoplasy).
review/2026-04-17/phase2_redteam_cycle11.md:40:### M3 — Primary anchor HIV-1 lacks the per-position validation HIV-1 failed in Ch5 Stage~1 Table
review/2026-04-17/phase2_redteam_cycle11.md:41:`ch5_discussion.tex:180–185` (Table tab:vaccine_escape Stage~1): HIV-1 Stage~1 enrichment = **0.35× with p=0.997** (below random). Stage~2 Contribution 3 now claims HIV-1 = 7.19× with Bonferroni p=2.5e-16 as the "primary external anchor." The reader is told in Ch1 that HIV-1 is the *primary* anchor with no reconciliation of why the Stage~1 HIV-1 number was worse than random. review/2026-04-17/phase2_redteam_cycle11.md:43:### M4 — 4-feature core and 98% claim have a confidence-interval problem
review/2026-04-17/phase2_redteam_cycle11.md:44:`ch4_results.tex:769–771,915`; `ch5_discussion.tex:250`; `ch6_conclusion.tex:25,139`. Ch4:770 admits MCC 0.081 vs 0.083 is within subsampling variability ±0.002, i.e., statistically indistinguishable. The "98% of ensemble performance" phrasing (0.081/0.083=0.976) is arithmetically misleading because the *denominator* 0.083 is itself within noise of the 4-feature 0.081. Reporting a ratio of two noise-equivalent numbers as "98%" is a Type-2 overclaim.
review/2026-04-17/phase2_redteam_cycle11.md:46:### M5 — SARS-CoV-2 Contribution 3 tier is internally self-contradictory
review/2026-04-17/phase2_redteam_cycle11.md:47:`ch4_results.tex:13` calls SARS-CoV-2 "exploratory after correction"; `ch5_discussion.tex:195–196` says SARS-CoV-2 "does not survive Bonferroni correction and is reported as exploratory only"; yet `ch5_discussion.tex:180` Stage~1 table reports SARS-CoV-2 Stage~1 enrichment 4.90× with **p<0.0001** (significant). A committee will ask: if the Stage~1 single-scoring SARS-CoV-2 enrichment was highly significant, what happened in Stage~2 that made SARS-CoV-2 become "exploratory"? Answer would be winner's-curse across 780 combos — but this rebuttal is not stated adjacent to the "exploratory" label.
review/2026-04-17/phase2_redteam_cycle11.md:52:### M7 — Friedman W=0.037 "near-zero agreement" interpretation conflicts with the pathogen-adaptive conclusion
review/2026-04-17/phase2_redteam_cycle11.md:53:`ch4_results.tex:425–428`. "near-zero agreement" is given two interpretations by the authors themselves (universal poor performance or pathogen-dependence) and then the pathogen-dependent reading is chosen on the basis of LOPO gap 0.265. But C2 above established that the 0.265 gap is null-consistent (p≈0.25–0.28). If the gap cannot distinguish from null, it cannot be used to pick interpretation (2) over (1) either. The Friedman argument is circular.

review/2026-04-17/phase2_redteam_cycle11.md:89:The cycle 10→11 reframe (HIV-1 primary / H3N2 self-consistency / SARS exploratory; permutation-null 0.96; ω² 0.296 + 0.103 + 0.39 triplet; Bonferroni exact p; novel-only enrichment; 16-row limitations table) *is* defensively thorough but has **tipped into over-hedging**. Three symptoms: (i) every headline number now carries 3+ caveats (ω², BCa-CI, cluster-vs-naive, 20-type vs 6-category, modeled vs residual) that *individually* are correct but *collectively* obscure whether the conclusion is strong or weak; (ii) new terms ("modeled variance component", "primary external anchor", "self-consistency check") are used as if established but lack operational definitions (M1, C3); (iii) the Korean manuscript (ch4_results.tex Korean sections still at 9-pathogen/0.285) did not receive the same overhaul as English (C1). The cycle 1–9 damage was overclaiming; cycle 10 and the post-cycle-10 re-writes have moved the needle past "appropriately hedged" into "audience fatigue" — a committee reader is invited to triangulate three ρ values, two ω² values, two pathogen counts, and a four-way permutation audit before reaching the actual finding. chapters/ch6_conclusion.tex:14:MutBench는 바이러스 변이 hotspot 검출을 위한 최초의 체계적 벤치마크 프레임워크를 도입하였으며, 3계층 ground truth(Layer A/B/C), hotspot-score 복합 지표, 합성 데이터 분석(1단계)과 9종 RNA 바이러스 대규모 비교(2단계)를 결합하는 2단계 실험 설계를 포함한다(상세 통계는 제~\ref{ch:results}장 참조).
chapters/ch6_conclusion.tex:20:셋째, Friedman 검정은 방법 간 성능 순위가 병원체에 따라 체계적으로 달라짐을 확인하였다.
chapters/ch6_conclusion.tex:21:넷째, Leave-One-Pathogen-Out(LOPO) 교차 검증에서 0/9 일치로, 훈련 병원체에서 선택한 최적 조합이 새로운 병원체에 일반화되지 않았다.
chapters/ch6_conclusion.tex:23:벤치마크 발견의 개념 증명 응용으로서, PAHD 프로토타입(제~\ref{subsec:pahd_prototype}절)은 게놈 프로파일 유사도가 탐지 패밀리 선호도를 부분적으로 예측할 수 있음을 보여주었다: v1 프로파일(8개 특성)은 5/9 양성 MCC, 중위수 MCC $= 0.014$(naive 중위수 $= 0.000$ 대비)를 달성하였고, v2 프로파일(85개 MSA 유래 특성)은 병리적 음의 전이를 제거하여 평균 MCC를 0.005에서 0.017로 개선하였다. 이는 벤치마크 결과가 실용적 방법 선택을 안내할 수 있음을 보여준다(상세 통계는 제~\ref{ch:results}장 참조).
chapters/ch6_conclusion.tex:39:DMS 데이터 4/9 병원체만 확보 & 중간 & 나머지 5종 Layer A+B 사용 & 신규 DMS 실험 \\
chapters/ch6_conclusion.tex:52:완전한 3계층 ground truth(Layer A, B, C)는 DMS 데이터가 확보된 4종의 병원체(SARS-CoV-2, H3N2, HIV-1, RSV)에 대해서만 이용 가능하며, 나머지 5종의 병원체는 Layer~A(수렴 진화)와 Layer~B(정제 선택)만으로 평가된다.
chapters/ch6_conclusion.tex:63:9종 RNA 바이러스(SARS-CoV-2, Influenza A/B, HIV-1, RSV, Dengue, HCV, MERS-CoV, Norovirus)에 대한 평가를 수행하였으나, DNA 바이러스(HPV, HBV 등)의 상이한 변이 메커니즘에 대한 검증은 아직 수행되지 않았다.
chapters/ch6_conclusion.tex:69:1단계 합성 벤치마크에서의 성능(hotspot-score 0.778)과 GISAID 실제 데이터에서의 성능 간에는 격차가 존재한다.
chapters/ch6_conclusion.tex:104:v1 Family-first 전략은 5/9 양성 MCC, 중위수 MCC $= 0.014$(naive 중위수 $= 0.000$ 대비)를 달성하였고; v2 프로파일은 더 판별적인 병원체 유사도 점수를 통해 병리적 음의 전이를 제거하여(예: HCV $-0.291 \rightarrow +0.141$) 평균 MCC를 0.005에서 0.017로 개선하였다.
chapters/ch6_conclusion.tex:105:그러나 정확 일치율은 v1과 v2 모두에서 0/9로 유지되어, 85개 특성을 사용하더라도 $n = 9$ 병원체의 근본적 한계가 지속됨을 확인하였다.
chapters/ch6_conclusion.tex:106:더 거친 예측 단위---탐지 패밀리(14개 패밀리)와 스코어링 공식(9개 공식)---에서 평가할 때, 일치율은 역시 0/9이었으나 달성된 MCC는 실질적으로 개선되었다: 패밀리 수준 예측은 oracle 성능의 48.3\%(평균 MCC $= 0.144$)를, 스코어링 수준 예측은 57.7\%(평균 MCC $= 0.172$)를 회복하여, 정확한 조합 예측(oracle의 1.7\%)을 크게 능가하였다.
chapters/ch6_conclusion.tex:115:계통발생학적 보정은 주로 강한 창시자 효과를 가진 병원체에 영향을 미칠 것이며(예: SARS-CoV-2 D614G, H-score 순위 2위이나 homoplasy 순위 1,134위), 해당 병원체의 최적 스코어링--탐지 조합을 변경하고 전체 oracle MCC를 개선할 가능성이 있다.
chapters/ch6_conclusion.tex:138:본 학위논문은 바이러스 변이 hotspot 검출을 위한 최초의 체계적 벤치마킹 프레임워크인 MutBench를 제시하고, 9종 RNA 바이러스에 대한 대규모 벤치마크 평가(총 3,159개 평가, 통계 검정에는 비영 MCC 2,418개 사용)를 통해 단일 최적 방법이 존재하지 않음을 통계적으로 입증하였다.
chapters/ch6_conclusion.tex:141:탐지 방법 성능이 방법 자체가 아닌 방법--병원체 상호작용($\omega^2 = 0.285$)에 의해 지배된다는 발견은 바이러스 유전체학을 넘어 더 넓은 함의를 가진다: 이질적인 입력 분포에 걸쳐 알고리즘이 적용되는 모든 도메인에서, 숨겨진 상호작용 효과를 노출하고 원칙적인 알고리즘 선택을 안내하기 위한 유사한 체계적 벤치마킹이 유익할 수 있다.
chapters/ch6_conclusion.tex:148:병원체 서열 데이터는 NCBI GenBank에서 수집하였으며, SARS-CoV-2 DMS 데이터는 Dadonaite 등~\cite{dadonaite2023dms}에서 제공된 원본 데이터를 사용하였다.

review/2026-04-17/phase1_blueteam.md:13:### Core Claim 1 — scoring × pathogen interaction is the dominant variance source (ω² = 0.296)
review/2026-04-17/phase1_blueteam.md:15:Claim: The choice of biological information source, conditional on pathogen, explains more of the MCC variance than any main effect or other interaction; therefore performance is governed by pathogen-specific information fit, not by scoring or detection algorithm in isolation.
review/2026-04-17/phase1_blueteam.md:17:- Evidence A — [Ch4:Sec 4.4.3 — three-way ANOVA] ch4_results.tex:368 Table~\ref{tab:9pathogen_anova} reports scoring×pathogen ω²=0.296, pathogen 0.117, family×pathogen 0.082, scoring 0.063, scoring×family 0.039, family 0.013. ch4:390 restates this as the single largest variance source under Cohen's ω²>0.14 threshold. **Strength: strong** (direct quantification, full factorial design over 8,580 cells).
review/2026-04-17/phase1_blueteam.md:18:- Evidence B — [Ch4:Sec 4.4.5 — ANOVA diagnostics and robustness] ch4_results.tex:471–473: cluster bootstrap over 11 pathogens gives 95% CI [0.195, 0.333]; HCV-excluded sensitivity gives ω²=0.246; Kruskal–Wallis non-parametric confirms all effects. **Strength: medium–strong** (addresses both sampling uncertainty and ground-truth atypicality, but the CI lower bound 0.195 is only ~39% above Cohen's large-effect threshold 0.14, so the "dominance" claim has real residual fragility if the 11 pathogens are not representative).
review/2026-04-17/phase1_blueteam.md:20:- Argument gap: **Layer C variance decomposition is never run.** The dissertation states Layer-C best scoring differs from Layer-A in 6/6 DMS pathogens (ch4_results.tex:525–533, Table~\ref{tab:layer_a_vs_c}), but does not re-run ANOVA on Layer-C MCC. Without this, the claim "ω²_scoring×pathogen=0.296" rides entirely on Layer-A, and the reader cannot see whether the interaction dominance survives a fully frequency-independent ground truth. This is the single largest defendable-on-retreat gap for Claim 1.
review/2026-04-17/phase1_blueteam.md:23:### Core Claim 2 — 11 pathogens all need different optimal combinations (LOPO 0/11)
review/2026-04-17/phase1_blueteam.md:25:Claim: The training-best scoring–detection combination from 10 pathogens never equals the oracle combination on the held-out 11th, and the mean MCC gap (0.265) is large in practical terms; therefore a single universal pipeline cannot be recommended.
review/2026-04-17/phase1_blueteam.md:27:- Evidence A — [Ch4:Sec 4.4.3 LOPO] ch4_results.tex:403–406: 0/11 match, mean generalization MCC 0.032, mean gap 0.265. Supported by Table~\ref{tab:9pathogen_best} ch4:276–293 showing 9 distinct scoring types across 11 unique combinations. **Strength: strong** for the descriptive claim (the numbers are direct counts from the CSV per Phase-0 check 3(d)).
review/2026-04-17/phase1_blueteam.md:28:- Evidence B — [Ch4:Sec 4.4.3 Friedman] ch4_results.tex:421–428: χ²=7.69, p=0.990, Kendall's W=0.037 across the top 20 combinations. **Strength: medium** — non-significance is intrinsically weak evidence; the text (ch4:427–429) explicitly states two interpretations (universally poor vs pathogen-dependent) and chooses the second based on the LOPO gap.
review/2026-04-17/phase1_blueteam.md:29:- Falsifiability: Claim fails if (a) 0/11 is the expected outcome under random assignment (null permutation test), (b) LOPO itself is ill-conditioned for n=11, or (c) a coarser predictor (family-level or scoring-formula-level) recovers matches.
review/2026-04-17/phase1_blueteam.md:31:  - (i) ch4:300–301 concedes that under 780 possible scoring–detection combinations, the random probability of 11 unique picks is ~93%, and ch5_discussion.tex:286 repeats this for 280 combinations (82%). The paper correctly pivots to "mean gap 0.265" as the real content — but the gap itself is never compared to a permutation null (what's the mean gap under random oracle draws?). Without that null, "large gap" is a qualitative assertion.
review/2026-04-17/phase1_blueteam.md:32:  - (ii) ch5_discussion.tex:317 explicitly admits the n=11 LOPO has two interpretations (truly adaptive vs underpowered). The paper argues (1) is right based on gap size, but does not power-analyze how many pathogens are needed before 0/11→k/11 for any realistic k.
review/2026-04-17/phase1_blueteam.md:33:  - (iii) Claim reframing risk: If a reviewer argues "0/11 means all methods are bad" (ch4:427 interpretation 1), the defense rests on oracle MCC range 0.196–0.660 (ch4:280–290). But three pathogens sit at MCC 0.196–0.211 (SARS-CoV-2, RSV, MERS), which a hostile reviewer can spin as "nearly as bad as the generalized 0.032." review/2026-04-17/phase_lit_consistency_cycle12.md:26:**Claim 1 (broadest benchmark) is the most exposed to direct conflict.** ViroGym (arXiv:2603.06740, Mar 2026) covers 13 virus types and 79 DMS assays plus 21 influenza neutralisation tasks; EVEREST v3 (bioRxiv 2025.08.04.668549v3, Jan 2026) covers 40 WHO-prioritized viruses across 16 viral families. MutBench's 11 RNA viruses with 8,580 hotspot evaluations is no longer the broadest in pathogen count, although the *task* (per-region binary hotspot detection with multi-source scoring × detector factorial) remains distinct from ViroGym/EVEREST's per-mutation Spearman regression. The paper already acknowledges this distinction in ch2 (Table 2.2) and ch5 L92, but the introduction and abstract still imply broadest-systematic-coverage framing that is now textually misleading. **Action**: re-frame "broadest" claims as "broadest under the per-region hotspot detection task with multi-source scoring × detector factorial design", and explicitly cite ViroGym/EVEREST-v3 as larger pathogen panels under different tasks.
review/2026-04-17/phase_lit_consistency_cycle12.md:28:**Claim 2 (scoring × pathogen interaction as largest variance component) is genuinely novel** in its formal ω² decomposition for viral hotspot benchmarks. EVEREST and ProteinGym report qualitatively that method performance varies across viruses/proteins, but neither runs a factorial ANOVA partition. MutBench is the first to provide a quantitative variance decomposition; the framing as "novel" is defensible.
review/2026-04-17/phase_lit_consistency_cycle12.md:30:**Claim 3 (LOPO 0/11, no universal best)** is consistent with — and quantitatively sharper than — prior qualitative findings in EVEREST ("no single model achieves consistent high performance"), ProteinGym (method×protein heterogeneity), and EVEscape (multi-source integration motivated by single-source insufficiency). MutBench's contribution is making this rigorously testable via LOPO + Friedman; the underlying claim is well-supported by external literature.
review/2026-04-17/phase_lit_consistency_cycle12.md:32:**Claim 4 (Layer A as hotspot proxy)** is well-validated by the homoplasy literature (SNPPar, ConDor, HomoplasyFinder), with one important caveat raised by bioRxiv 2021.05.15.444301: SARS-CoV-2 convergent evolution can be inferred unreliably from phylogenetic analyses. The entropy-quantile auxiliary inherits known Shannon-entropy saturability limitations (Veaf 2025); MutBench already acknowledges this in ch5 L47, L33–35. The Layer A construction is on solid biological footing.
review/2026-04-17/phase_lit_consistency_cycle12.md:34:**Claim 5 (3-tier evidence hierarchy)** is borrowed from clinical-trial methodology (FDA Multiple Endpoints Guidance) and is **not standard in bioinformatics benchmarking** (Weber 2019, Mangul 2019 do not use this framing). MutBench's adaptation of primary / self-consistency / exploratory to vaccine-escape sub-claims is a defensible methodological innovation but should be explicitly flagged as such — currently the dissertation uses these terms operationally without crediting the clinical-trial source or explaining the adaptation.
review/2026-04-17/phase_lit_consistency_cycle12.md:36:**Cross-cutting recommendation**: Add a paragraph in ch2 §2.1.7 (or new §2.2) acknowledging ViroGym and EVEREST v3 as concurrent external benchmarks on the per-mutation prediction task, clarify that MutBench's 11-pathogen scope is broadest under the per-region hotspot detection × multi-source scoring factorial task, and cite Bretz/FDA endpoint hierarchy as the methodological inspiration for the 3-tier evidence framing.

review/2026-04-17/phase6_cycle13_ivv.md:40:> "A natural alternative for the small-n regime is *Bayesian hierarchical (partial-pooling) modeling*: with weakly informative priors on the pathogen-level variance components, the per-pathogen ω² estimates are shrunk toward the population mean by a factor that depends on the ratio of within- to between-pathogen variance. For the present design, a half-Cauchy prior on the between-pathogen scale and a uniform prior on the within-pathogen residual is the standard default; the resulting posterior interaction ω² would be expected to lie below the fixed-effect point estimate (0.296) with a credible interval that is wider than the cluster-bootstrap CI but still bounded above zero, since the cluster-bootstrap lower bound (0.195) already exceeds Cohen's large-effect threshold under aggressive resampling. A formal posterior fit is queued as future-work Priority 5; the directional conclusion (interaction ≫ 0) is not in question, only the precise magnitude."

review/2026-04-17/phase_alternative_cycle6.md:130:## 3A. 9.36× enrichment는 H3N2 HA의 구조적 특성(작은 단백질 + 조밀한 antigenic site)의 산물
review/2026-04-17/phase_alternative_cycle6.md:132:**가설**: H3N2 HA는 543 AA, 29개 antigenic 위치가 Sites A/B에 집중. Protein이 작고 target이 조밀하면 어떤 detector도 높은 enrichment 달성 가능.
review/2026-04-17/phase_alternative_cycle6.md:134:**논문 대응**: 없음. Ch4:860은 FUBAR의 생물학적 해석을 제시하나 H3N2 자체의 구조적 편중을 배제하지 않음.
review/2026-04-17/phase_alternative_cycle6.md:139:- H3N2: L=543, n_escape=29 → max-possible enrichment = 543/29 ≈ 18.7×. Observed 9.36× = **50% of theoretical ceiling**.
review/2026-04-17/phase_alternative_cycle6.md:140:- SARS-CoV-2: L=1273, n_escape=30 → ceiling = 42.4×. Observed top 13.99× = 33% of ceiling.
review/2026-04-17/phase_alternative_cycle6.md:141:- HIV-1: L=856, n_escape=45 → ceiling = 19.0×. Observed 7.19× = 37% of ceiling.
review/2026-04-17/phase_alternative_cycle6.md:142:- **즉 H3N2가 유독 높은 enrichment 달성한 것은 그 자체의 target density로 일부 설명 가능** (ceiling의 50% 도달). 하지만 SARS-CoV-2와 HIV-1도 ceiling 대비 30–37% 달성하므로 detector가 일관되게 작동 중.
review/2026-04-17/phase_alternative_cycle6.md:146:- 각 pathogen에서 top detector가 FUBAR 계열인지, 아니면 pathogen별로 다른지 확인 (SARS-CoV-2 → rare_freq/tranception, HIV-1 → freq/dnds_proxy) — 이미 다르므로 "H3N2만 특이"가 아님을 강조하는 방향으로 기술 가능.
